title.zh: 卷一百七十二 列傳第五十九: 程鉅夫 趙孟頫 鄧文原 袁桷 曹元用 齊履謙
title.en: Volume 172 Biographies 59: Cheng Jufu, Zhao Mengfu, Deng Wenyuan, Yuan Jue, Cao Yuanyong, Qi Luqian
title.raw: 卷一百七十二 列傳第五十九: 程鉅夫 趙孟頫 鄧文原 袁桷 曹元用 齊履謙 Volume 172 Biographies 59: Cheng Jufu, Zhao Mengfu, Deng Wenyuan, Yuan Jue, Cao Yuanyong, Qi Luqian

sentences.zh: 程鉅夫

translations.literal: Cheng Jufu
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Jufu

sentences.zh: 程鉅夫，名文海，避武宗廟諱，以字行。

translations.literal: Cheng Jufu, personal name Wenhai; to avoid the temple taboo name of Emperor Wuzong, he was known by his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Jufu, whose personal name was Wenhai, went by his style name to avoid the taboo of Emperor Wuzong's temple name.

sentences.zh: 其先自徽州徙郢州京山，後家建昌。

translations.literal: His ancestors moved from Huizhou to Jingshan in E Prefecture, and later the family settled in Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had moved from Huizhou to Jingshan in Ezhou, and the family later made its home in Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 叔父飛卿，仕宋，通判建昌，世祖時，以城降。

translations.literal: His uncle Feiqing served the Song as vice prefect of Jianchang; in the time of Emperor Shizu, he surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Feiqing had served the Song as vice prefect of Jianchang and, in the reign of Kublai, surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 鉅夫入為質子，授宣武將軍、管軍千戶。

translations.literal: Jufu entered [the capital] as a hostage, and was appointed Xuanwu General and commander of a thousand-household military unit.
translations.idiomatic: Jufu was sent to court as a hostage and appointed Xuanwu General with command of a thousand-household unit.

sentences.zh: 他日，召見，問賈似道何如人，鉅夫條對甚悉，帝悅，給筆札書之，乃書二十餘幅以進。

translations.literal: Another day he was summoned for an audience; the emperor asked what sort of man Jia Sidao was. Jufu answered item by item in great detail. The emperor was pleased, gave him brush and paper to write it down, and he wrote more than twenty sheets and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he was summoned and asked what manner of man Jia Sidao was. Jufu replied in careful detail, and the emperor, pleased, supplied brush and paper; he wrote out more than twenty sheets and submitted them.

sentences.zh: 帝大奇之，因問今居何官，以千戶對，帝謂近臣曰：「朕觀此人相貌，已應貴顯；

translations.literal: The emperor greatly marveled at him and then asked what office he presently held; he answered that of thousand-household commander. The emperor said to his close attendants: "I observe this man's appearance—he already ought to attain high eminence;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply impressed and asked what post he currently held; he replied, thousand-household commander. The emperor told his close attendants, "Judging by this man's looks, he is already destined for high rank;

sentences.zh: 聽其言論，誠聰明有識者也。

translations.literal: hearing his discourse, he is truly intelligent and perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: and to hear him speak, he is truly bright and discerning.

sentences.zh: 可置之翰林。」

translations.literal: He may be placed in the Hanlin Academy."
translations.idiomatic: He should be placed in the Hanlin Academy."

sentences.zh: 丞相火禮霍孫傳旨至翰林，以其年少，奏為應奉翰林文字，帝曰：「自今國家政事得失，及朝臣邪正，宜皆為朕言之。」

translations.literal: The Chancellor Huo Zali transmitted the decree to the Hanlin; because he was young, [Huo] memorialized appointing him Attendant Literary Official of the Hanlin. The emperor said: "From now on, the gains and losses of state affairs, and whether court ministers are upright or corrupt—you should all report them to Us."
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Huo Zali relayed the order to the Hanlin, and because Jufu was young, recommended him as Attendant Literary Official of the Hanlin. The emperor said, "From now on you are to tell me the rights and wrongs of state policy and which ministers are upright or corrupt."

sentences.zh: 鉅夫頓首謝曰：「臣本疏遠之臣，蒙陛下知遇，敢不竭力以報陛下！」

translations.literal: Jufu bowed his head in thanks and said: "Your subject was originally a remote and distant official; receiving Your Majesty's gracious notice, how would I dare not exert my utmost strength to repay Your Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: Jufu kowtowed and said, "I was only a humble outsider until Your Majesty singled me out; how could I fail to serve you with all my strength!"

sentences.zh: 尋進翰林修撰，屢遷集賢直學士，兼秘書少監。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was promoted to Hanlin Compiler, and repeatedly advanced to Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Hanlin Compiler, then repeatedly advanced to Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies while also serving as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至元十九年，奏陳五事：一曰取會江南仕籍，二曰通南北之選，三曰立考功歷，四曰置貪贓籍，五曰給江南官吏俸。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan, he memorialized presenting five matters: first, to gather and reconcile the official registers of the south; second, to open selection between north and south; third, to establish records of merit evaluation; fourth, to set up a register of corruption and bribery; fifth, to grant salaries to officials of the south.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 19 he submitted five proposals: reconcile southern official registers; open appointments across north and south; establish merit-evaluation records; keep a register of corrupt officials; and pay salaries to southern officials.

sentences.zh: 朝廷多采行之。

translations.literal: The court largely adopted and carried them out.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted most of these measures.

sentences.zh: 賜地京師安貞門，以築居室。

translations.literal: He was granted land at Anzhen Gate in the capital to build a residence.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted land at Anzhen Gate in the capital on which to build a home.

sentences.zh: 二十年，加翰林集賢直學士，同領會同館事。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he was additionally made Hanlin Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and jointly directed the affairs of the Hall of United Submission.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he was further made Hanlin Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and jointly oversaw the Hall of United Submission.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，見帝，首陳：「興建國學，乞遣使江南搜訪遺逸；

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, on seeing the emperor, he first stated: "Establish the National University; I beg that envoys be sent to the south to search out and invite reclusive talents;
translations.idiomatic: In year 23, when he saw the emperor, he urged first of all: "Found a National University and send envoys to the south to seek out hidden scholars;

sentences.zh: 御史臺、按察司，並宜參用南北之人。」

translations.literal: the Censorate and the surveillance commissions should alike employ men from both north and south."
translations.idiomatic: and both the Censorate and the surveillance commissions should employ men from north and south alike."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor welcomed and accepted these proposals.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，立尚書省，詔以為參知政事，鉅夫固辭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the Ministry of Works was established; he was ordered to be Vice Director of the Secretariat, but Jufu firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24, when the Ministry of Works was established, he was ordered to serve as vice director of the Secretariat, but Jufu firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 又命為御史中丞，台臣言：「鉅夫南人，且年少。」

translations.literal: He was again ordered to be Censor-in-Chief; censorial officials said: "Jufu is a southerner, and moreover young."
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed censor-in-chief, but censorial officials objected: "Jufu is a southerner and still young."

sentences.zh: 帝大怒曰：「汝未用南人，何以知南人不可用！

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and said: "You have not yet employed southerners—how do you know southerners cannot be used!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage: "You have never employed southerners—how can you know they are unfit!

sentences.zh: 自今省部台院，必參用南人。」

translations.literal: From now on the ministries, departments, censorate, and academies must employ southerners in combination."
translations.idiomatic: From now on every ministry, department, censorate, and academy must include southerners."

sentences.zh: 遂以鉅夫仍為集賢直學士，拜侍御史，行御史臺事，奉詔求賢於江南。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jufu was still made Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, appointed Attending Censor, and exercised the affairs of the Censorate, receiving an edict to seek worthies in the south.
translations.idiomatic: Jufu was then kept on as Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, appointed attending censor with charge of censorial affairs, and sent south by imperial order to recruit talent.

sentences.zh: 初，書詔令皆用蒙古字，及是，帝特命以漢字書之。

translations.literal: At first, edicts and orders were all written in Mongol script; on this occasion the emperor specially ordered them written in Chinese characters.
translations.idiomatic: Previously all edicts had been written in Mongol script, but this time the emperor expressly ordered them written in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 帝素聞趙孟藡、葉李名，鉅夫臨當行，帝密諭必致此二人；

translations.literal: The emperor had long heard the names of Zhao Mengfu and Ye Li; as Jufu was about to depart, the emperor secretly instructed that these two men must be brought.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long known the reputations of Zhao Mengfu and Ye Li, and as Jufu was about to leave, privately told him he must bring those two men back.

sentences.zh: 鉅夫又薦趙孟頫、余恁、萬一鶚、張伯淳、胡夢魁、曾晞顏、孔洙、曾衝子、凌時中、包鑄等二十餘人，帝皆擢置台憲及文學之職。

translations.literal: Jufu also recommended Zhao Mengfu, Yu Ren, Wan Yie, Zhang Bochun, Hu Mengkui, Zeng Xiyan, Kong Zhu, Zeng Chongzi, Ling Shizhong, Bao Zhu, and more than twenty others; the emperor all promoted them to censorial and literary posts.
translations.idiomatic: Jufu also recommended Zhao Mengfu, Yu Ren, Wan Yie, Zhang Bochun, Hu Mengkui, Zeng Xiyan, Kong Zhu, Zeng Chongzi, Ling Shizhong, Bao Zhu, and more than twenty others, all of whom the emperor placed in censorial or literary offices.

sentences.zh: 還朝，陳民間利病五事，拜集賢學士，仍還行臺。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he presented five matters of benefit and harm among the people; he was appointed Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and still returned to the regional censorate.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he laid out five points of popular grievance and benefit, was made Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, and again took up duty at the regional censorate.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，時相桑哥專政，法令苛急，四方騷動。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, the chief minister Sangge monopolized government; laws and orders were harsh and urgent, and the four quarters were in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 the chief minister Sangge dominated the government; his laws were harsh and unrest spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 鉅夫入朝，上疏曰：「臣聞天子之職，莫大於擇相，宰相之職，莫大於進賢。

translations.literal: Jufu entered court and submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has heard that among the Son of Heaven's duties none is greater than choosing a chancellor, and among a chancellor's duties none is greater than advancing the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Jufu came to court and memorialized: "I have heard that a ruler's greatest duty is to choose his chancellor, and a chancellor's greatest duty is to advance worthy men.

sentences.zh: 苟不以進賢為急，而惟以殖貨為心，非為上為德、為下為民之意也。

translations.literal: If one does not make advancing the worthy urgent but only has amassing goods at heart, this is not the intent of serving above with virtue and serving below for the people.
translations.idiomatic: If one does not treat advancing talent as urgent but sets his heart only on amassing wealth, that is not the meaning of ruling with virtue above and caring for the people below.

sentences.zh: 昔文帝以決獄及錢穀問丞相周勃，勃不能對，陳平進曰：'陛下問決獄，責廷尉；

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen asked Chancellor Zhou Bo about deciding cases and about grain and money; Bo could not answer. Chen Ping stepped forward and said: 'If Your Majesty asks about deciding cases, hold the Commandant of Justice responsible;
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Wen of Han asked Chancellor Zhou Bo about trials and about grain revenues; Zhou Bo could not answer. Chen Ping stepped forward and said, 'If Your Majesty asks about trials, that is the Commandant of Justice's affair;

sentences.zh: 問錢穀，責治粟內史。

translations.literal: if Your Majesty asks about grain and money, hold the Grand Herald responsible for grain.
translations.idiomatic: if Your Majesty asks about grain revenues, that is the Grand Herald's affair.

sentences.zh: 宰相上理陰陽，下遂萬物之宜，外鎮撫四夷，內親附百姓。

translations.literal: A chancellor above regulates yin and yang, below brings all things to their proper course, outwardly pacifies the four barbarians, inwardly draws the hundred surnames close.'
translations.idiomatic: A chancellor harmonizes heaven and earth above, helps all things find their proper place below, pacifies the border peoples abroad, and keeps the common people close at home.'

sentences.zh: '觀其​​所言，可以知宰相之職矣。

translations.literal: Observing what he said, one can know the chancellor's duties.
translations.idiomatic: From what he said one can see what a chancellor's duty truly is.

sentences.zh: 今權奸用事，立尚書鉤考錢穀，以剝割生民為務，所委任者，率皆貪饕邀利之人，江南盜賊竊發，良以此也。

translations.literal: Now a powerful traitor holds office; the Ministry of Revenue was established to audit grain and money, making stripping and cutting the living people its task. Those entrusted are mostly greedy, rapacious men who seek profit; bandits in the south have quietly risen—truly because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Today a powerful favorite holds sway: the Ministry of Revenue was set up to audit revenues and treats fleecing the people as its business. Those he appoints are almost all greedy profiteers, and it is precisely for this reason that banditry has broken out across the south.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以為宜清尚書之政，損行省之權，罷言利之官，行恤民之事，於國為便。」

translations.literal: Your subject ventures to think it fitting to clarify the Ministry of Revenue's government, reduce the regional secretariats' power, abolish profit-seeking offices, and carry out measures to comfort the people—this would benefit the state."
translations.idiomatic: I believe the state would benefit if the Ministry of Revenue were reformed, provincial powers reduced, profit-seeking offices abolished, and measures to relieve the people carried out."

sentences.zh: 桑哥大怒，羈留京師不遣，奏請殺之，凡六奏，帝皆不許。

translations.literal: Sangge was greatly enraged, detained him in the capital and would not send him away, and memorialized requesting his execution—six memorials in all—but the emperor each time did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Sangge was furious, kept him in the capital, and six times memorialized for his execution, but each time the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 鉅夫既還行臺，二十九年，又召鉅夫與胡祗遹、姚燧、王憚、雷膺、陳天祥、楊恭懿、高凝、陳儼、趙居信等十人，赴闕賜對。

translations.literal: After Jufu had returned to the regional censorate, in the twenty-ninth year he was again summoned together with Hu Zhiyuan, Yao Sui, Wang Yun, Lei Ying, Chen Tianxiang, Yang Gongyi, Gao Ning, Chen Yan, Zhao Juxin, and nine others—ten men in all—to come to court and receive imperial audience.
translations.idiomatic: After Jufu returned to the regional censorate, in year 29 he was summoned again with Hu Zhiyuan, Yao Sui, Wang Yun, Lei Ying, Chen Tianxiang, Yang Gongyi, Gao Ning, Chen Yan, Zhao Juxin, and nine others—ten men in all—for an imperial audience at court.

sentences.zh: 三十年，出為閩海道肅政廉訪使，興學明教，吏民畏愛之。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he went out as Surveillance Commissioner for the Minhai Circuit for Incorrupt Government, promoted schools and clarified teaching; officials and people both feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 30 he was posted as surveillance commissioner for the Minhai circuit, where he promoted schools and enlightened teaching; officials and commoners alike respected and cherished him.

sentences.zh: 大德四年，遷江南湖北道肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dade he was transferred to Surveillance Commissioner for the Jiangnan-Hubei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 4 he was transferred to surveillance commissioner for the Jiangnan-Hubei circuit.

sentences.zh: 至官，首治行省平章家奴之為民害者，上下肅然。

translations.literal: On reaching his post, he first punished the regional secretariat's chief minister's household slaves who were harming the people; above and below became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he first dealt with the chief minister's household slaves who were preying on the people, and order was restored throughout the administration.

sentences.zh: 八年，召拜翰林學士，商議中書省事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was summoned and appointed Hanlin Academician, deliberating on Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was recalled, made Hanlin Academician, and consulted on Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 十年，以亢旱、暴風、星變，鉅夫應詔陳弭災之策，其目有五：曰敬天，曰尊祖，曰清心，曰持體，曰更化。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, because of severe drought, violent wind, and astral anomalies, Jufu responded to an edict and presented strategies to quell calamity—five headings: revering Heaven, honoring ancestors, purifying the mind, maintaining personal discipline, and renewing transformation.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10, amid severe drought, violent storms, and celestial omens, Jufu answered an edict with five remedies: reverence for Heaven, honor for the ancestors, purity of mind, discipline of conduct, and renewal of policy.

sentences.zh: 帝皆然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved them all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved them all.

sentences.zh: 雲南省臣言：「世祖親平雲南，民願刻石點蒼山，以紀功德。」

translations.literal: Yunnan provincial officials said: "Emperor Shizu personally pacified Yunnan; the people wish to carve a stone on Diancang Mountain to record his merit."
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan officials said, "When Kublai personally pacified Yunnan, the people wished to carve a stone on Diancang Mountain to record his merit."

sentences.zh: 詔鉅夫撰其文。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jufu to compose the text.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Jufu to compose the inscription.

sentences.zh: 十一年，拜山南江北道肅政廉訪使，复留為翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner for the Shannan-Jiangbei Circuit, but was again retained as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he was appointed surveillance commissioner for the Shannan-Jiangbei circuit but was kept on again as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，修《成宗實錄》。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida he compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 1 he compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 二年，召至上都。

translations.literal: In the second year he was summoned to Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was summoned to Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 三年，復拜山南江北道肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was again appointed Surveillance Commissioner for the Shannan-Jiangbei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was again appointed surveillance commissioner for the Shannan-Jiangbei circuit.

sentences.zh: 四年，與李謙、尚文等十六人同赴闕，賜對便殿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, together with Li Qian, Shang Wen, and fourteen others—sixteen men in all—he came to court and was granted audience in the side hall.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he went to court with Li Qian, Shang Wen, and fourteen others—sixteen in all—and was granted audience in the side hall.

sentences.zh: 拜浙東海右道肅政廉訪使，留為翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: He was appointed Surveillance Commissioner for the Zhedong-Haiyou Circuit, but was retained as Chief Academician of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed surveillance commissioner for the Zhedong-Haiyou circuit but was kept on as chief Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，修《武宗實錄》。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Wuzong.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangqing 1 he compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 二年，旱，鉅夫應詔陳桑林六事，忤時宰意。

translations.literal: In the second year there was drought; Jufu responded to an edict and presented six matters of the Mulberry Grove, offending the chief minister's intent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, during a drought, Jufu answered an edict with six proposals on drought relief, which displeased the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 明日，帝遣近侍賜上尊，勞之曰：「中書集議，惟卿所言甚當，後臨事，其極言之。」

translations.literal: The next day the emperor sent a close attendant to bestow fine wine and comfort him, saying: "When the Secretariat gathered to deliberate, only your words were very fitting; hereafter when you face affairs, speak to the utmost."
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor sent a close attendant with fine wine and told him, "In the Secretariat discussion only your views were right; speak your mind fully whenever you are involved in affairs."

sentences.zh: 於是詔鉅夫偕平章政事李孟、參知政事許師敬議行貢舉法，鉅夫建言：「經學當主程頤、硃熹傳注，文章宜革唐、宋宿弊。」

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Jufu together with Chief Minister Li Meng and Vice Director Xu Shijing to deliberate on implementing the examination system. Jufu proposed: "Classical learning should take the commentaries transmitted by Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi as primary; literary composition should reform the long-standing abuses of Tang and Song."
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Jufu, together with Chief Minister Li Meng and Vice Director Xu Shijing, to draft the civil-service examination system. Jufu proposed, "Classical studies should follow the commentarial tradition of Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi, and literary composition should break with Tang and Song abuses."

sentences.zh: 命鉅夫草詔行之。

translations.literal: He ordered Jufu to draft an edict and put it into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Jufu was ordered to draft the edict implementing these reforms.

sentences.zh: 三年，以病乞骸骨歸田裡，不允，命尚醫給藥物，官其子大本郊祀署令，以便侍養。

translations.literal: In the third year, on grounds of illness he requested his bones and return to his home village; it was not granted. He was ordered the Imperial Physicians to supply medicines, and his son Daben was given office as Director of the Suburban Sacrifice Office so he might conveniently attend and support him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he asked to retire home on grounds of illness, but was refused; imperial physicians were ordered to supply medicine, and his son Daben was made director of the suburban sacrifice office so he could remain nearby to care for him.

sentences.zh: 時令近臣撫視，且勞之曰：「卿世祖舊臣，惟忠惟貞，其勉加粥，少留京師，以副朕心。」

translations.literal: From time to time he ordered close attendants to visit and comfort him, saying: "You are an old minister of Shizu, loyal and steadfast only; strive to take more gruel, stay a while longer in the capital, to fulfill Our heart."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regularly sent close attendants to inquire after him and said, "You are an old servant of Kublai, loyal and steadfast; take good care of yourself, stay a little longer in the capital, and ease my mind."

sentences.zh: 鉅夫請益堅，特授光祿大夫，賜上尊，命廷臣以下飲餞於齊化門外，給驛南還。

translations.literal: Jufu's request grew still firmer; he was specially granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, given fine wine, and ordered that court ministers and below drink a farewell toast outside Qihua Gate; post-horses were provided for his return south.
translations.idiomatic: Jufu pressed his request all the more firmly, so he was specially made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, given fine wine, and the court was ordered to give him a farewell banquet outside Qihua Gate before he was sent south by post relay.

sentences.zh: 敕行省及有司常加存問。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the regional secretariat and relevant offices regularly to inquire after his welfare.
translations.idiomatic: The regional secretariat and local offices were ordered to inquire regularly after his welfare.

sentences.zh: 居三年而卒，年七十。

translations.literal: After three years' residence he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died, at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 泰定二年，贈大司徒、柱國，追封楚國公，諡文憲。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiding he was posthumously granted Grand Mentor and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed as Duke of Chu, with posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiding 2 he was posthumously made Grand Mentor and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed as Duke of Chu, with the posthumous title Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 趙孟頫

translations.literal: Zhao Mengfu
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Mengfu

sentences.zh: 趙孟頫，字子昂，宋太祖子秦王德芳之後也。

translations.literal: Zhao Mengfu, style name Zi'ang, was a descendant of Prince Qin Defang, son of Emperor Taizu of the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Mengfu, styled Zi'ang, was descended from Prince Qin Defang, a son of Song Taizu.

sentences.zh: 五世祖秀安僖王子偁，四世祖崇憲靖王伯圭。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor was Prince Xiuan of the fifth rank, Zicheng; his fourth-generation ancestor was Prince Chongxian of the fourth rank, Bogui.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor was Prince Xiuan, Zicheng; his fourth-generation ancestor was Prince Chongxian, Bogui.

sentences.zh: 高宗無子，立子偁之子，是為孝宗，伯圭，其兄也，賜第於湖州，故孟頫湖州人。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong had no son and established Zicheng's son, who became Emperor Xiaozong. Bogui was his elder brother; a mansion was granted at Huzhou, hence Mengfu was a man of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong had no heir, he enthroned Zicheng's son as Emperor Xiaozong; Bogui was Xiaozong's elder brother, and because the family was granted a mansion at Huzhou, Mengfu was considered a native of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖師垂，祖希永，父與訔，仕宋，皆至大官；

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Shichui, his grandfather Xiyong, his father Yuyin; all served the Song and reached high office;
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shichui, grandfather Xiyong, and father Yuyin all served the Song and rose to high office;

sentences.zh: 入國朝，以孟頫貴，累贈師垂集賢侍讀學士，希永太常禮儀院使，並封吳​​興郡公，與訔集賢大學士，封魏國公。

translations.literal: entering the present dynasty, because of Mengfu's eminence they were repeatedly enfeoffed posthumously: Shichui as Reader-in-Waiting of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, Xiyong as Commissioner of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, both enfeoffed as Dukes of Wuxing Commandery; Yuyin as Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: after the dynasty changed, Mengfu's standing brought them repeated posthumous honors: Shichui as reader-in-waiting of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and Duke of Wuxing; Xiyong as commissioner of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Duke of Wuxing; and Yuyin as grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 孟頫幼聰敏，讀書過目輒成誦，為文操筆立就。

translations.literal: Mengfu was clever and keen from youth; when he read a book he could recite it after one look, and when he wrote he took up the brush and finished at once.
translations.idiomatic: Mengfu was exceptionally bright as a boy: he could recite a text after a single reading and compose essays as soon as he took up the brush.

sentences.zh: 年十四，用父廕補官，試中吏部銓法，調真州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he used his father's privilege to obtain office, passed the Ministry of Personnel's selection examination, and was transferred to be Registrar of the Revenue Section in Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he entered office through his father's privilege, passed the Ministry of Personnel examination, and was appointed registrar in the revenue section at Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宋亡，家居，益自力於學。

translations.literal: When the Song perished he lived at home and applied himself all the more vigorously to learning.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Song he lived in retirement and devoted himself even more intensely to study.

sentences.zh: 至元二十三年，行臺侍御史程鉅夫奉詔搜訪遺逸於江南，得孟頫，以之入見。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Zhiyuan, Attending Censor of the Regional Censorate Cheng Jufu received an edict to search out reclusive talents in the south, obtained Mengfu, and brought him to audience.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 23, Cheng Jufu of the regional censorate, sent south to seek hidden scholars, found Mengfu and brought him to court.

sentences.zh: 孟頫才氣英邁，神采煥發，如神仙中人，世祖顧之喜，使坐右丞葉李上。

translations.literal: Mengfu's talent and spirit were lofty and expansive, his bearing radiant, like a transcendent being; Emperor Shizu looked at him with pleasure and had him seated above Right Vice Director Ye Li.
translations.idiomatic: Mengfu's brilliance and bearing were radiant, almost otherworldly; Kublai was delighted and seated him above Right Vice Director Ye Li.

sentences.zh: 或言孟頫宋宗室子，不宜使近左右，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Someone said Mengfu was a son of the Song imperial clan and ought not be kept near the emperor's side; the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Some said that as a Song imperial clansman he should not be kept close to the throne, but the emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 時方立尚書省，命孟頫草詔頒天下，帝覽之，喜曰：「得朕心之所欲言者矣。」

translations.literal: At that time the Ministry of Revenue was being established; he ordered Mengfu to draft an edict to promulgate throughout the realm. The emperor read it and said with pleasure: "You have obtained what Our heart wished to say."
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Ministry of Revenue was being established, and Mengfu was ordered to draft the edict promulgated empire-wide. The emperor read it and said with delight, "This says exactly what I wished to say."

sentences.zh: 詔集百官於刑部議法，眾欲計至元鈔二百貫​​贓滿者死，孟頫曰：「始造鈔時，以銀為本，虛實相權，今二十餘年間，輕重相去至數十倍，故改中統為至元，又二十年後，至元必復如中統，使民計鈔抵法，疑於太重。

translations.literal: An edict gathered all officials at the Ministry of Justice to deliberate on law; the multitude wished to reckon bribery at two hundred strings of Zhiyuan paper money as the threshold for death. Mengfu said: "When paper money was first created, silver was the standard and emptiness and fullness were mutually weighted; now in more than twenty years light and heavy have differed by as much as tenfold, hence Zhongtong was changed to Zhiyuan; after another twenty years Zhiyuan will certainly again be like Zhongtong—making the people reckon paper money against the law seems perhaps too heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were summoned to the Ministry of Justice to revise the penal code; most favored death for bribery reaching two hundred strings of Zhiyuan notes. Mengfu objected: "Paper money was originally backed by silver, with nominal and real value kept in balance, but in twenty-odd years their relative weight has shifted tenfold, which is why Zhongtong notes were replaced by Zhiyuan notes. In another twenty years Zhiyuan notes will depreciate just as Zhongtong notes did, so tying capital crimes to note values seems far too harsh.

sentences.zh: 古者以米、絹民生所須，謂之二實，銀、錢與二物相權，謂之二虛。

translations.literal: In antiquity rice and silk, what the people's livelihood required, were called the two realities; silver and cash were mutually weighted against the two things and called the two emptinesses.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity rice and silk, the staples of daily life, were called the two real values, while silver and coin, exchangeable against them, were called the two nominal values.

sentences.zh: 四者為直，雖升降有時，終不大相遠也，以絹計贓，最為適中。

translations.literal: The four served as standards; though they rose and fell at times, in the end they did not greatly diverge—reckoning bribery by silk is most moderate.
translations.idiomatic: These four served as standards; though their relative values shifted, they never diverged wildly, so calculating bribery in silk would be the most balanced measure.

sentences.zh: 況鈔乃宋時所創，施於邊郡，金人襲而用之，皆出於不得已。

translations.literal: Moreover paper money was created in Song times, applied in border commanderies; the Jurchens adopted and used it—all from unavoidable necessity.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, paper money was a Song invention, used on the frontiers and adopted by the Jurchens—all measures born of necessity.

sentences.zh: 乃欲以此斷人死命，似不足深取也。」

translations.literal: Yet to wish to use this to decide men's lives in death seems not quite sufficient to take deeply."
translations.idiomatic: To make it the basis for capital punishment seems hardly a sound foundation."

sentences.zh: 或以孟頫年少，初自南方來，譏國法不便，意頗不平，責孟頫曰：「今朝廷行至元鈔，故犯法者以是計贓論罪。

translations.literal: Someone, because Mengfu was young and had newly come from the south, mocked that the national law was inconvenient and was rather displeased, reproaching Mengfu: "Now the court implements Zhiyuan paper money, therefore offenders are reckoned for bribery and judged by crime thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Someone, taking offense that a young newcomer from the south should criticize state policy, rebuked him: "The court now uses Zhiyuan notes, so offenders are judged by note values—that is the law.

sentences.zh: 汝以為非，豈欲沮格至元鈔耶？」

translations.literal: You think it wrong—do you wish to obstruct Zhiyuan paper money?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you mean to obstruct the Zhiyuan currency?"

sentences.zh: 孟頫曰：「法者人命所繫，議有重輕，則人不得其死矣。

translations.literal: Mengfu said: "Law is what men's lives depend on; if deliberation has heavy and light, then people will not obtain their proper death.
translations.idiomatic: Mengfu replied, "Law concerns human life; if penalties are debated as light or heavy, people will not receive justice in death.

sentences.zh: 孟頫奉詔與議，不敢不言。

translations.literal: Mengfu received the edict to join deliberation and dared not fail to speak.
translations.idiomatic: I was ordered to take part in this deliberation and could not remain silent.

sentences.zh: 今中統鈔虛，故改至元鈔，謂至元鈔終無虛時，豈有是理！

translations.literal: Now Zhongtong paper money was empty, hence it was changed to Zhiyuan paper money—to say Zhiyuan paper money will never have an empty time, is there such a principle!
translations.idiomatic: Zhongtong notes depreciated, so they were replaced by Zhiyuan notes—to claim Zhiyuan notes will never depreciate is absurd!

sentences.zh: 公不揆於理，欲以勢相陵，可乎！」

translations.literal: You, sir, do not measure by reason but wish to overwhelm by power—is that permissible!"
translations.idiomatic: If you will not reason with me but only try to overwhelm me by rank, is that acceptable!"

sentences.zh: 其人有愧色。

translations.literal: That man had a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: The man flushed with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 帝初欲大用孟頫，議者難之。

translations.literal: The emperor at first wished to employ Mengfu greatly; deliberators made difficulties.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at first wished to give Mengfu high office, but critics objected.

sentences.zh: 二十四年六月，授兵部郎中。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year 24 he was appointed director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 兵部總天下諸驛，時使客飲食之費，幾十倍於前，吏無以供給，強取於民，不勝其擾，遂請於中書，增鈔給之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War oversaw all post stations in the realm; at that time envoys' food and drink costs were nearly ten times what they had been before; clerks had nothing with which to supply them and forcibly took from the people, unable to bear the harassment, so they requested of the Secretariat increased paper money allotments.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War oversaw the empire's post stations; envoy hospitality costs had risen nearly tenfold, and clerks, unable to meet them, extorted the people until the burden became unbearable, so they asked the Secretariat for increased note allotments.

sentences.zh: 至元鈔法滯澀不能行，詔遣尚書劉宣與孟頫馳驛至江南，問行省丞相慢令之罪，凡左右司官及諸路官，則徑笞之。

translations.literal: The Zhiyuan paper-money law was sluggish and obstructed and could not be implemented; an edict dispatched Minister Liu Xuan and Mengfu by fast post to the south, to inquire into the regional secretariat chief minister's crime of delaying orders; as for all left and right secretariat officials and circuit officials, they were to be flogged directly.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhiyuan currency policy stalled, Liu Xuan of the Ministry and Mengfu were sent post-haste to the south to investigate the regional chief minister for delaying orders, with authority to flog secretariat and circuit officials on the spot.

sentences.zh: 孟頫受命而行，比還，不笞一人，丞相桑哥大以為譴。

translations.literal: Mengfu received the order and went; when he returned he had flogged not a single person; Chief Minister Sangge greatly took it as a reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Mengfu carried out the mission but flogged no one on his return, to Sangge's great displeasure.

sentences.zh: 時有王虎臣者，言平江路總管趙全不法，即命虎臣往按之。

translations.literal: At that time there was Wang Huchen, who said the Pingjiang Circuit chief administrator Zhao Quan acted unlawfully; he was immediately ordered to send Huchen to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Huchen reported that Zhao Quan, chief administrator of Pingjiang circuit, was corrupt, and the court immediately ordered Wang to investigate.

sentences.zh: 葉李執奏不宜遣虎臣，帝不聽，孟頫進曰：「趙全固當問，然虎臣前守此郡，多強買人田，縱賓客為奸利，全數與爭，虎臣怨之。

translations.literal: Ye Li firmly memorialized that Huchen ought not be sent; the emperor did not listen. Mengfu advanced and said: "Zhao Quan indeed should be questioned, but Huchen formerly governed this commandery, forcibly bought many people's fields, and let guests and clients commit illicit profit; Quan repeatedly disputed with him and Huchen bears resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Li memorialized that Wang should not be sent, but the emperor refused to listen. Mengfu said, "Zhao Quan should indeed be investigated, but Wang once governed this circuit, forcibly bought land, and let his clients profit illicitly; he and Zhao Quan clashed repeatedly, and Wang bears a grudge.

sentences.zh: 虎臣往，必將陷全，事縱得實，人亦不能無疑。」

translations.literal: If Huchen goes he will certainly frame Quan; even if the matter proves true, people still cannot be without doubt."
translations.idiomatic: If Wang is sent he is sure to frame Zhao Quan; even if the charges prove true, people will still doubt the outcome."

sentences.zh: 帝悟，乃遣他使。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and thereupon sent another envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and sent another investigator instead.

sentences.zh: 桑哥鐘初鳴時即坐省中，六曹官後至者，則笞之，孟頫偶後至，斷事官​​遽引孟頫受笞，孟俯入訴於都堂右丞葉李曰：「古者刑不上大夫，所以養其廉恥，教之節義，且辱士大夫，是辱朝廷也。」

translations.literal: Sangge when the bell first sounded already sat in the ministry; officials of the six bureaus who arrived late were flogged. Mengfu happened to arrive late; the deciding official hastily led Mengfu to receive flogging. Mengfu entered and appealed to Right Vice Director Ye Li in the chief hall, saying: "In antiquity punishment did not reach grand masters—that was to nurture their integrity and shame and teach them moderation and righteousness; moreover, to humiliate scholar-officials is to humiliate the court."
translations.idiomatic: Sangge was already at his desk when the first bell rang, and latecomers among the six bureaus were flogged. Mengfu happened to arrive late and was hurried off to be beaten. He appealed to Ye Li: "In antiquity punishment did not reach high officials, so as to preserve their honor and teach them integrity; to humiliate scholar-officials is to humiliate the court itself."

sentences.zh: 桑哥亟慰孟頫使出，自是所笞，唯曹史以下。

translations.literal: Sangge quickly comforted Mengfu and had him leave; from then on those flogged were only clerks and below.
translations.idiomatic: Sangge quickly soothed him and sent him out; thereafter only clerks and lower staff were flogged.

sentences.zh: 他日，行東御牆外，道險，孟頫馬跌墮於河。

translations.literal: Another day, traveling outside the eastern imperial wall, the road was perilous; Mengfu's horse stumbled and fell into a river.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, while traveling along the road outside the eastern palace wall, Mengfu's horse stumbled on the dangerous path and plunged into a river.

sentences.zh: 桑哥聞之，言於帝，移築禦牆稍西二丈許。

translations.literal: Sangge heard of it, spoke to the emperor, and had the imperial wall rebuilt shifted slightly westward by about two zhang.
translations.idiomatic: When Sangge heard of it, he reported to the emperor and had the palace wall moved roughly two zhang to the west.

sentences.zh: 帝聞孟頫素貧，賜鈔五十錠。

translations.literal: The emperor heard Mengfu had always been poor and bestowed fifty ingots of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Mengfu had long lived in poverty, the emperor granted him fifty ingots of paper money.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，遷集賢直學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, he was transferred to Direct Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was appointed Direct Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 是歲地震，北京尤甚，地陷，黑沙水湧出，人死傷數十萬，帝深憂之。

translations.literal: That year there was an earthquake; Beijing suffered especially severely—the ground subsided, black sand and water gushed forth, and hundreds of thousands died or were injured; the emperor was deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: That year an earthquake struck, Beijing hardest; the ground sank, black sand and water burst forth, and hundreds of thousands were killed or wounded. The emperor was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 時駐蹕龍虎台，遣阿剌渾撒里馳還，召集賢、翰林兩院官，詢致災之由。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was encamped at Longhu Platform; he dispatched Araghun Saris to ride back posthaste and summon officials of the Academies of Gathered Worthies and Hanlin, inquiring the cause of the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then encamped at Longhu Platform and sent Araghun Saris riding back in haste to summon Academicians from the Hanlin and Gathered Worthies academies and ask what had caused the disaster.

sentences.zh: 議者畏忌桑哥，但泛引《經》、傳及五行災異之言，以修人事、應天變為對，莫敢語及時政。

translations.literal: Those who deliberated feared Sangge; they only broadly cited the Classics, commentaries, and Five-Elements disaster portents, answering with improving human affairs and responding to heaven's changes—and none dared speak of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: Those who deliberated feared Sangge and would cite only vague passages from the Classics and commentaries about the Five Elements and heavenly omens, advising moral reform to answer heaven's warning—and none dared mention current affairs.

sentences.zh: 先是，桑哥遣忻都及王濟等理算天下錢糧，已徵入數百萬，未徵者尚數千萬，害民特甚，民不聊生，自殺者相屬，逃山林者，則發兵捕之，皆莫敢沮其事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Sangge had sent Xindu and Wang Ji and others to audit all revenue grain throughout the empire; already collected were several millions, while uncollected still amounted to several tens of millions; the harm to the people was extreme, the people could not make a living, suicides followed one after another; those who fled to mountains and forests had troops sent to capture them—and none dared obstruct the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sangge had dispatched Xindu, Wang Ji, and others to audit land tax and grain levies empire-wide. Hundreds of millions had already been collected, yet tens of millions remained unpaid; the burden on the people was terrible—they could barely survive, suicides came one after another, and those fleeing to the hills were hunted by troops. No one dared stand in the way.

sentences.zh: 孟頫與阿剌渾撒里甚善，勸令奏帝赦天下，盡與蠲除，庶幾天變可弭。

translations.literal: Mengfu was on very good terms with Araghun Saris and urged him to memorialize the emperor to pardon the empire and fully grant remission, so that perhaps the heavenly change might be appeased.
translations.idiomatic: Mengfu was close to Araghun Saris and urged him to ask the emperor for a general pardon and full remission of outstanding levies, so that heaven's wrath might perhaps be stilled.

sentences.zh: 阿剌渾撒里入奏，如孟頫所言，帝從之。

translations.literal: Araghun Saris entered and memorialized as Mengfu had said; the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: Araghun Saris did as Mengfu advised and presented the memorial; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔草已具，桑哥怒謂必非帝意。

translations.literal: The draft edict was already prepared; Sangge angrily said it certainly was not the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Once the draft edict was ready, Sangge angrily insisted it could not reflect the emperor's true wishes.

sentences.zh: 孟頫曰：「凡錢糧未徵者，其人死亡已盡，何所從取？

translations.literal: Mengfu said: "Of all revenue grain not yet collected, the debtors are already dead—whence is it to be taken?
translations.idiomatic: Mengfu said, "For all unpaid levies, the debtors are already dead to the last man—where are you going to collect from?

sentences.zh: 非及是時除免之，他日言事者，倘以失陷錢糧數千萬歸咎尚書省，豈不為丞相深累耶！」

translations.literal: If not at this time to remit and exempt, later when men speak on affairs, if they should blame the Ministry of Revenue for the loss of several tens of millions in revenue grain, would this not deeply burden the chief counselor!"
translations.idiomatic: If you don't cancel it now, later critics will blame the Ministry of Revenue for losing tens of millions in uncollected revenue—and won't that fall heavily on you as chief counselor?"

sentences.zh: 桑哥悟，民始獲蘇。

translations.literal: Sangge understood; the people only then obtained relief.
translations.idiomatic: Sangge saw the point, and the people at last found relief.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問葉李、留夢炎優劣，孟頫對曰：「夢炎，臣之父執，其人重厚，篤於自信，好謀而能斷，有大臣器；

translations.literal: The emperor once asked about the relative merits of Ye Li and Liu Mengyan; Mengfu replied: "Mengyan is my father's friend; the man is weighty and solid, deeply self-assured, fond of planning yet able to decide—he has the capacity of a great minister;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked Mengfu to compare Ye Li and Liu Mengyan. He replied, "Mengyan, a friend of my father Zhao Yuyin, is steady and self-assured, thoughtful yet decisive—he has the makings of a great minister;

sentences.zh: 葉李所讀之書，臣皆讀之，其所知所能，臣皆知之能之。」

translations.literal: the books Ye Li has read, I have all read; what he knows and can do, I all know and can do."
translations.idiomatic: as for the books Ye Li has read, I have read them all; whatever he knows and can do, I know and can do as well."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝以夢炎賢於李耶？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Do you consider Mengyan more worthy than Li?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Do you think Mengyan is the better man?

sentences.zh: 夢炎在宋為狀元，位至丞相，當賈似道誤國罔上，夢炎依阿取容；

translations.literal: Mengyan in the Song was chief graduate, rose to chief counselor; when Jia Sidao misled the state and deceived his sovereign, Mengyan fawned and sought favor;
translations.idiomatic: Mengyan was Song's top examination graduate and rose to chief counselor, yet when Jia Sidao misled the realm and deceived the throne, he fawned and played for favor;

sentences.zh: 李布衣，乃伏闕上書，是賢於夢炎也。

translations.literal: Li was a commoner in plain clothes, yet submitted a memorial at the palace gate—that is worthier than Mengyan.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Li was only a common scholar, yet he knelt at the palace gate with a memorial—that makes him the worthier man.

sentences.zh: 汝以夢炎父友，不敢斥言其非，可賦詩譏之。」

translations.literal: You, taking Mengyan as your father's friend, dare not openly speak his fault—compose a poem to satirize him."
translations.idiomatic: Because Mengyan was your father's friend you won't speak plainly against him—then write a poem to satirize him instead."

sentences.zh: 孟頫所賦詩，有「往事已非那可說，且將忠直報皇元」之語，帝歎賞焉。

translations.literal: In the poem Mengfu composed were the lines "The past is gone—what need to speak of it? Let loyal straightness repay Great Yuan"; the emperor sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Mengfu's poem included the lines, "The past cannot be undone—why speak of it? Let loyalty and integrity repay the Yuan." The emperor sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 孟頫退謂奉御徹里曰：「帝論賈似道誤國，責留夢炎不言，桑哥罪​​甚於似道，而我等不言，他日何以辭其責！

translations.literal: Mengfu withdrew and said to Palace Attendant Cheli: "The emperor spoke of Jia Sidao misleading the state and blamed Liu Mengyan for not speaking; Sangge's crime is even greater than Sidao's—yet we say nothing; how in days to come shall we excuse our responsibility!
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Mengfu told the palace attendant Cheli, "The emperor spoke of Jia Sidao's ruin of the state and faulted Liu Mengyan for his silence—but Sangge's crimes exceed Sidao's, and we say nothing. How will we answer for that one day?

sentences.zh: 然我疏遠之臣，言必不聽，侍臣中讀書知義理，慷慨有大節，又為上所親信，無逾公者。

translations.literal: Yet I am a distant and remote minister; if I speak, it will certainly not be heard. Among attending ministers, one who reads books and knows principle and righteousness, is magnanimous with great integrity, and is also trusted by the sovereign—none surpasses you.
translations.idiomatic: But I am far from the emperor's inner circle—if I speak, he won't listen. Among the attendants, none reads the classics, knows what's right, has the courage to act on principle, and enjoys the emperor's trust as you do.

sentences.zh: 夫損一旦之命，為萬姓除殘賊，仁者之事也。

translations.literal: To sacrifice one morning's life to remove cruel villains for ten thousand commoners—that is the affair of the benevolent.
translations.idiomatic: To risk one's life to rid the people of a tyrant—that is what a man of benevolence should do.

sentences.zh: 公必勉之！」

translations.literal: You must surely exert yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: You must take this on!"

sentences.zh: 既而徹里至帝前，數桑哥罪惡，帝怒，命衛士批其頰，血涌口鼻，委頓地上。

translations.literal: Shortly after, Cheli came before the emperor and enumerated Sangge's crimes; the emperor was angry and ordered guards to strike his cheeks; blood gushed from nose and mouth and he collapsed on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Cheli went before the emperor and listed Sangge's crimes. The emperor flew into a rage and had the guards strike his face until blood poured from his nose and mouth and he crumpled to the floor.

sentences.zh: 少間，复呼而問之，對如初。

translations.literal: After a short while, [the emperor] again summoned and questioned him; he answered as at first.
translations.idiomatic: A little later the emperor summoned him again and questioned him; Cheli answered just as before.

sentences.zh: 時大臣亦有繼言者，帝遂按誅桑哥，罷尚書省，大臣多以罪去。

translations.literal: At the time great ministers also spoke up in succession; the emperor thereupon investigated and executed Sangge, abolished the Ministry of Revenue, and many great ministers were dismissed for crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Other high officials joined in, and the emperor had Sangge investigated and executed, abolished the Ministry of Revenue, and dismissed many ministers on charges of corruption.

sentences.zh: 帝欲使孟頫與聞中書政事，孟頫固辭，有旨令出入宮門無禁。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to have Mengfu participate in hearing Zhongshu Secretariat affairs; Mengfu firmly declined; an edict ordered him free entry and exit through palace gates without restriction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted Mengfu involved in central secretariat business, but Mengfu firmly declined. An edict nonetheless granted him unrestricted access through the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 每見，必從容語及治道，多所裨益。

translations.literal: Each time they met, [the emperor] would leisurely discourse on the way of governing, benefiting much.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they met, the emperor would speak at ease about governance, and Mengfu's counsel proved of great benefit.

sentences.zh: 帝問：「汝趙太祖孫耶？

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "Are you a grandson of Emperor Taizu of Zhao?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Are you descended from Emperor Taizu of Zhao?

sentences.zh: 太宗孫耶？」

translations.literal: A grandson of Emperor Taizong?"
translations.idiomatic: Or from Emperor Taizong?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣太祖十一世孫。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Your servant is an eleventh-generation descendant of Taizu."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I am Taizu's eleventh-generation descendant."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「太祖行事，汝知之乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Do you know Taizu's conduct?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Do you know how Taizu governed?"

sentences.zh: 孟頫謝不知，帝曰：「太祖行事，多可取者，朕皆知之。」

translations.literal: Mengfu apologized that he did not know; the emperor said: "Much in Taizu's conduct is worth taking—I know it all."
translations.idiomatic: Mengfu demurred that he did not. The emperor said, "Much of what Taizu did is worth emulating—I know it well."

sentences.zh: 孟頫自念久在上側，必為人所忌，力請補外。

translations.literal: Mengfu thought to himself that long at the sovereign's side, he would surely be envied by others, and strenuously requested appointment outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Mengfu worried that staying so long at the emperor's side would invite jealousy, and he pressed hard for a provincial appointment.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，出同知濟南路總管府事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he went out as vice director of Jinan Circuit Chief Administrator's office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed vice administrator of Jinan circuit.

sentences.zh: 時總管闕，孟頫獨署府事，官事清簡。

translations.literal: At the time the chief administrator post was vacant; Mengfu alone signed office affairs; official business was clear and simple.
translations.idiomatic: The chief administrator's post was vacant, so Mengfu alone handled the prefecture's affairs, which were few and straightforward.

sentences.zh: 有元掀兒者，役於鹽場，不勝艱苦，因逃去。

translations.literal: There was one Yuan Xian'er, serving corvée labor at a salt works, unable to bear the hardship, who therefore fled.
translations.idiomatic: A laborer named Yuan Xian'er, pressed into service at a salt works, could bear the hardship no longer and fled.

sentences.zh: 其父求得他人屍，遂誣告同役者殺掀兒，既誣服。

translations.literal: His father obtained another person's corpse and then falsely accused fellow laborers of killing Xian'er; they had already been coerced into confessing.
translations.idiomatic: The father obtained someone else's corpse and falsely accused Xian'er's fellow laborers of murder; they had already been forced to confess.

sentences.zh: 孟頫疑其冤，留弗決。

translations.literal: Mengfu suspected injustice and withheld decision.
translations.idiomatic: Mengfu suspected a miscarriage of justice and held the case open.

sentences.zh: 踰月，掀兒自歸，郡中稱為神明。

translations.literal: After a month, Xian'er returned of himself; the commandery called it divine discernment.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Xian'er returned on his own, and the district hailed Mengfu as divinely perceptive.

sentences.zh: 僉廉訪司事韋哈剌哈孫，素苛虐，以孟頫不能承順其意，以事中之。

translations.literal: Concurrent Intendant for Rectification Wei Qalghasun was by nature harsh and cruel; because Mengfu could not comply with his wishes, he framed him on a matter.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qalghasun, commissioner of the surveillance commission, was notoriously cruel; resenting Mengfu's refusal to defer to him, he tried to incriminate him on a petty charge.

sentences.zh: 會修《世祖實錄》，召孟頫還京師，乃解。

translations.literal: It happened that the Veritable Records of Emperor Shizu was being compiled; Mengfu was summoned back to the capital, and the matter was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: When work began on Emperor Shizu's Veritable Records, Mengfu was recalled to the capital and the charge was dropped.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷知汾州，未上，有旨書金字《藏經》，既成，除集賢直學士、江浙等處儒學提舉，遷泰州尹，未上。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was transferred to know Fen Prefecture; before taking up the post, there was a decree to write the gold-letter Buddhist Canon; when it was completed, he was appointed Direct Academician of Gathered Worthies and Educational Intendant for Jiangzhe and other regions, transferred to Prefect of Taizhou—but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed prefect of Fenzhou but had not yet reported when he was ordered to copy the Buddhist canon in gold ink. When that was finished he was made Direct Academician of Gathered Worthies and Educational Intendant for Jiangzhe, then Prefect of Taizhou—but again he did not take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 至大三年，召至京師，以翰林侍讀學士，與他學士撰定祀南郊祝文，及擬進殿名，議不合，謁告去。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhida, summoned to the capital, as Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician, together with other academicians he drafted the prayer text for sacrifice at the Southern Suburban Altar and proposed hall names; opinions did not agree and he requested leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 3 he was summoned to the capital as Hanlin Attendant Reader and, with other scholars, drafted the southern suburban sacrifice prayers and proposed names for palace halls; when opinions clashed he asked leave and left.

sentences.zh: 仁宗在東宮，素知其名，及即位，召除集賢侍講學士、中奉大夫。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong in the Eastern Palace had long known his reputation; when he ascended the throne, he summoned and appointed him Gathered Worthies Attendant Lecturer Academician and Zhongfeng Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong had known Mengfu's reputation since his days as crown prince; on acceding he appointed him Gathered Worthies Attendant Lecturer and Zhongfeng Grandee.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，改翰林侍講學士，遷集賢侍講學士、資德大夫。

translations.literal: First year of Yanyou: changed to Hanlin Attendant Lecturer Academician; transferred to Gathered Worthies Attendant Lecturer Academician, Zide Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 1 he became Hanlin Attendant Lecturer, then Gathered Worthies Attendant Lecturer with the rank of Zide Grandee.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜翰林學士承旨、榮祿大夫。

translations.literal: Third year: appointed Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief, Ronglu Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief with the rank of Ronglu Grandee.

sentences.zh: 帝眷之甚厚，以字呼之而不名。

translations.literal: The emperor favored him very deeply, calling him by style name and not by personal name.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored him deeply and addressed him by his style name rather than his personal name.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗與侍臣論文學之士，以孟頫比唐李白、宋蘇子瞻。

translations.literal: The emperor once with attending ministers discussed men of literary accomplishment, comparing Mengfu to Li Bai of Tang and Su Zizhan of Song.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once discussed literary giants with his attendants and compared Mengfu to Li Bai of Tang and Su Shi of Song.

sentences.zh: 又嘗稱孟頫操履純正，博學多聞，書畫絕倫，旁通佛、老之旨，皆人所不及。

translations.literal: He also once praised Mengfu's conduct as pure and upright, his learning broad and hearing many, his calligraphy and painting unmatched, and his penetrating understanding of Buddhist and Daoist principles—all beyond what others could reach.
translations.idiomatic: He also praised Mengfu's moral integrity, vast learning, peerless calligraphy and painting, and grasp of Buddhist and Daoist teaching—surpassing all others.

sentences.zh: 有不悅者間之，帝初若不聞者。

translations.literal: Those who were displeased slandered him between; at first the emperor seemed not to hear.
translations.idiomatic: Envious officials tried to turn the emperor against him, but at first he seemed not to notice.

sentences.zh: 又有上書言國史所載，不宜使孟頫與聞者，帝乃曰：「趙子昂，世祖皇帝所簡拔，朕特優以禮貌，置於館閣，典司述作，傳之後世，此屬呶呶何也！」

translations.literal: Again there was one who memorialized that what the national history recorded ought not have Mengfu participate; the emperor then said: "Zhao Ziang was selected and elevated by Emperor Shizu; I especially honor him with courtesy and place him in the academies to oversee composition for transmission to later ages—what is all this nagging about!"
translations.idiomatic: When someone memorialized that Mengfu should not be involved in compiling the national history, the emperor said, "Zhao Ziang was personally selected by Kublai; I honor him with special courtesy and place him in the academies to oversee historical writing for posterity—what is all this petty carping!"

sentences.zh: 俄賜鈔五百錠，謂侍臣曰：「中書每稱國用不足，必持而不與，其以普慶寺別貯鈔給之。」

translations.literal: Shortly after, he bestowed five hundred ingots of paper money, telling attending ministers: "The Secretariat always says state funds are insufficient and surely holds back and will not give—take it from the separately stored paper money at Puqing Temple and give it to him."
translations.idiomatic: He soon granted five hundred ingots of paper money, telling his attendants, "The Secretariat always pleads empty coffers and refuses payment—take it from the special store at Puqing Temple."

sentences.zh: 孟頫嘗累月不至宮中，帝以問左右，皆謂其年老畏寒，敕禦府賜貂鼠裘。

translations.literal: Mengfu once went many months without coming to the palace; the emperor asked those around him; all said he was old and feared cold; an edict ordered the imperial store to bestow a sable and marten fur coat.
translations.idiomatic: When Mengfu stayed away from court for months, the emperor asked his attendants why; they said the old man feared the cold, and the emperor ordered the imperial wardrobe to send him a sable coat.

sentences.zh: 初，孟頫以程鉅夫薦，起家為郎，及鉅夫為翰林學士承旨，求致仕去，孟頫代之，先往拜其門，而後入院，時人以為衣冠盛事。

translations.literal: Initially, Mengfu through Cheng Jufu's recommendation began his career as a court gentleman; when Jufu became Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief and sought retirement, Mengfu replaced him; he first went to pay respects at his gate, then afterward entered the academy—contemporaries regarded it a splendid ceremony of the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: Mengfu had entered service through Cheng Jufu's recommendation; when Jufu retired as Hanlin Expositor-in-Chief, Mengfu succeeded him, first paying a formal visit to Jufu's home before taking his seat—an occasion people hailed as a crowning ritual of scholar-official decorum.

sentences.zh: 六年，得請南歸。

translations.literal: Sixth year: obtained permission to return south.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was granted leave to return south.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使賜衣幣，趣之還朝，以疾，不果行。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys bestowing robes and silks, urging him to return to court; due to illness, he did not in the end go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys with robes and gifts urging his return, but illness prevented him from going.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，英宗遣使即其家俾書《孝經》。

translations.literal: First year of Zhizhi: Emperor Yingzong sent envoys to his home ordering him to write out the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizhi 1, Emperor Yingzong sent envoys to his home to have him copy out the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 二年，賜上尊及衣二襲。

translations.literal: Second year: bestowed imperial wine and two sets of robes.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he received imperial wine and two sets of robes.

sentences.zh: 是歲六月卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: That year in the sixth month he died, age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died that sixth month at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 追封魏國公，諡文敏。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, posthumous name Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Wei with the posthumous name Wenmin.

sentences.zh: 孟頫所著，有《尚書注》，有《琴原》、《樂原》，得律呂不傳之妙。

translations.literal: What Mengfu authored included Commentary on the Book of Documents, Origins of the Zither and Origins of Music, grasping the untransmitted subtleties of pitch and mode.
translations.idiomatic: Mengfu's writings included a commentary on the Book of Documents, Origins of the Zither and Origins of Music, works that captured the lost subtleties of musical pitch and mode.

sentences.zh: 詩文清邃奇逸，讀之使人有飄飄出塵之想。

translations.literal: His poetry and prose were clear, deep, strange, and unfettered; reading them gives one thoughts of drifting above the dust of the world.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose were lucid, profound, and wonderfully free; reading them lifts the mind above worldly cares.

sentences.zh: 篆、籀、分、隸、真、行、草書，無不冠絕古今，遂以書名天下。

translations.literal: Seal, great-seal, clerical, official, regular, running, and cursive scripts—none were not foremost and unmatched through past and present; thus he became famous throughout the realm for calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: In seal, great-seal, clerical, official, regular, running, and cursive scripts he stood unmatched in any age, and his name became synonymous with calligraphy throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 天竺有僧，數萬里來求其書歸，國中寶之。

translations.literal: There was a monk from India who came tens of thousands of li to seek his writing and take it home; his country treasured it.
translations.idiomatic: A monk from India traveled tens of thousands of li to obtain his calligraphy and carry it home, where his country treasured it as a treasure.

sentences.zh: 其畫山水、木石、花竹、人馬，尤精緻。

translations.literal: His paintings of mountains and water, trees and rocks, flowers and bamboo, men and horses were especially refined.
translations.idiomatic: His landscapes, trees and rocks, flowers and bamboo, and figures with horses were especially exquisite.

sentences.zh: 前史官楊載稱孟頫之才頗為書畫所掩，知其書畫者，不知其文章，知其文章者，不知其經濟之學。

translations.literal: Former historiographer Yang Zai said Mengfu's talent was rather overshadowed by calligraphy and painting: those who knew his calligraphy and painting did not know his literary writings; those who knew his literary writings did not know his statecraft learning.
translations.idiomatic: The former historiographer Yang Zai observed that Mengfu's brilliance was largely eclipsed by his calligraphy and painting: admirers of his brushwork overlooked his prose, and readers of his prose overlooked his mastery of statecraft.

sentences.zh: 人以為知言云。

translations.literal: People considered this apt words.
translations.idiomatic: People judged that a keen observation.

sentences.zh: 子雍、奕，並以書畫知名。

translations.literal: Sons Yong and Yi both were renowned for calligraphy and painting.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yong and Yi both became known for calligraphy and painting.

sentences.zh: 鄧文原

translations.literal: Deng Wenyuan
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wenyuan

sentences.zh: 鄧文原，字善之，一字匪石，綿州人。

translations.literal: Deng Wenyuan, style name Shanzi, another style Feishi, was a native of Mian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wenyuan, styled Shanzi and also known as Feishi, was a native of Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 父漳，徙錢塘。

translations.literal: His father Zhang moved to Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang moved the family to Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 文原年十五，通《春秋》。

translations.literal: Wenyuan at age fifteen had mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: By fifteen Wenyuan had mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 在宋時，以流寓試浙西轉運司，魁四川士。

translations.literal: In Song times, as a sojourner he tested at the Zhexi Transport Commission and ranked first among Sichuan scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song, though living as a sojourner, he took the examination of the Zhexi Transport Commission and ranked first among candidates from Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 至元二十七年，行中書省辟為杭州路儒學正。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Zhiyuan, the Branch Secretariat recruited him as Confucian Administrator of Hangzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 27 the Branch Secretariat appointed him Confucian Administrator of Hangzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 大德二年，調崇德州教授。

translations.literal: Second year of Dade: transferred as Instructor of Chongde Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 2 he was transferred to serve as instructor in Chongde prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: Fifth year: promoted to Hanlin Document Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to Hanlin Document Attendant.

sentences.zh: 九年，升修撰，謁告還江南。

translations.literal: Ninth year: promoted to Compiler; requested leave and returned to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to Compiler, then asked leave and returned to Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，復為修撰，預修《成宗實錄》。

translations.literal: First year of Zhida: again served as Compiler, participating in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 1 he again served as Compiler and helped compile Emperor Chengzong's Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 三年，授江浙儒學提舉。

translations.literal: Third year: appointed Educational Intendant for Jiangzhe Confucian schools.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed Educational Intendant for Jiangzhe.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，召為國子司業。

translations.literal: First year of Huangqing: summoned as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangqing 1 he was summoned to serve as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 至官，首建白更學校之政，當路因循，重於改作，論不合，移病去。

translations.literal: Upon reaching his post, he first memorialized to reform school policy; those in charge were conservative, attaching weight to not changing established arrangements; opinions did not agree; he submitted illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he immediately proposed reforms to school administration, but local authorities were set in their ways and resisted change; when they could not agree he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 科舉制行，文原校文江浙，慮士守舊習，大書硃熹《貢舉私議》，揭於門。

translations.literal: When the civil examination system was implemented, Wenyuan graded papers in Jiang-Zhe; fearing scholars clung to old habits, he wrote out in large characters Zhu Xi's Private Opinions on the Examinations and posted it at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the civil service examinations were instituted, Wenyuan graded papers in Jiang-Zhe; fearing candidates would cling to old habits, he posted Zhu Xi's Private Opinions on the Examinations in large characters at the gate.

sentences.zh: 延祐四年，升翰林待制。

translations.literal: Fourth year of Yanyou: promoted to Hanlin Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 4 he was promoted to Hanlin Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 五年，出僉江南浙西道肅政廉訪司事，平江僧有憾其府判官理熙者，賄其徒，告熙贓，熙誣服。

translations.literal: Fifth year: went out as Concurrent Intendant for the Jiangnan and Zhexi Circuit Surveillance and Rectification Commission; a monk in Pingjiang who bore a grudge against its prefectural judge Li Xi bribed his followers to accuse Xi of corruption, and Xi was coerced into confessing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed concurrent commissioner of the Jiangnan and Zhexi Surveillance Commission. A Pingjiang monk who resented the prefectural judge Li Xi bribed his followers to accuse Xi of corruption, and Xi was forced to confess.

sentences.zh: 文原行部，按問得實，杖僧而釋熙。

translations.literal: Wenyuan on circuit inspection investigated and obtained the truth; he flogged the monk and released Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan investigated on his tour of duty, established the facts, had the monk flogged, and released Li Xi.

sentences.zh: 吳興民夜歸，巡邏者執之，系亭下。

translations.literal: A commoner of Wuxing returned home at night; patrol guards seized him and bound him beneath a pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: A man from Wuxing was returning home at night when patrol guards seized him and tied him beneath a pavilion.

sentences.zh: 其人遁去，有追及之者，刺其脅，僕地。

translations.literal: The man escaped; one who pursued and caught up stabbed him in the flank and he fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The man broke free, but a pursuer caught up and stabbed him in the side, and he collapsed.

sentences.zh: 明旦，家人得之以歸，比死，其兄問殺汝者何如人，曰：「白帽、青衣、長身者也。」

translations.literal: At dawn his family found him and brought him home; as he was dying, his elder brother asked what sort of man had killed him; he said: "One with a white cap, blue clothes, and a tall frame."
translations.idiomatic: At dawn his family found him and brought him home. As he lay dying, his elder brother asked what the killer looked like; he said, "A tall man in a white cap and blue robes."

sentences.zh: 其兄訴於官，有司問直初更者曰張福兒，執之，使服焉。

translations.literal: His elder brother complained to the authorities; the officials questioned the night-watchman on the first watch, who said Zhang Fu'er; they seized him and forced him to confess.
translations.idiomatic: His brother reported the crime. Officials questioned the first-watch patrolman, who named Zhang Fu'er; they arrested him and forced a confession.

sentences.zh: 械系三年，文原錄之曰：「福兒身不滿六尺，未見其長也；

translations.literal: Shackled and imprisoned for three years; Wenyuan recorded in the case, saying: "Fu'er's body is less than six chi—his tallness is not seen;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang had been shackled in prison for three years when Wenyuan reviewed the record and wrote, "Fu'er stands less than six chi tall—hardly a tall man;

sentences.zh: 刃傷右脅，而福兒素用左手，傷宜在左，何右傷也！」

translations.literal: the blade wound was on the right flank, yet Fu'er habitually uses his left hand—the wound ought to be on the left; why a wound on the right!"
translations.idiomatic: the blade struck the right flank, yet Fu'er is left-handed—the wound should be on the left. Why is it on the right?"

sentences.zh: 鞫之，果得真殺人者，而釋福兒。

translations.literal: On interrogation, the true killer was indeed obtained, and Fu'er was released.
translations.idiomatic: On re-examination he found the real killer and released Fu'er.

sentences.zh: 桐廬人戴汝惟家被盜，有司得盜，獄成送郡。

translations.literal: The home of Dai Ruwei of Tonglu was burglarized; the authorities caught the thief; the case was completed and sent to the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The home of Dai Ruwei of Tonglu was robbed; officials caught a thief, closed the case, and sent it to the prefectural court.

sentences.zh: 夜有焚戴氏廬者，而不知汝惟所之。

translations.literal: That night someone burned the Dai family's outbuildings, and no one knew where Ruwei had gone.
translations.idiomatic: That night someone set fire to the Dai family's outbuildings, and no one knew where Ruwei had gone.

sentences.zh: 文原曰：「此必有故也。」

translations.literal: Wenyuan said: "This must have a reason."
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan said, "There must be more to this."

sentences.zh: 乃得其妻葉氏與其弟謀殺汝惟狀，而於水涯樹下得屍，與漬血斧俱在焉，人以為神。

translations.literal: Thereupon he obtained the account of how Ruwei's wife, the Ye clan, and her younger brother plotted to kill Ruwei; beneath a tree at the water's edge he found the corpse, and a blood-soaked axe was there as well—people considered it divine discernment.
translations.idiomatic: He uncovered a plot by Ruwei's wife, née Ye, and her brother to murder him; at the water's edge beneath a tree he found the body and a blood-stained axe. People hailed his judgment as uncanny.

sentences.zh: 六年，移江東道。

translations.literal: Sixth year: transferred to the Jiangdong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to the Jiangdong circuit.

sentences.zh: 徽、寧國、廣德三郡，歲入茶課鈔三千錠，後增至十八萬錠，竭山谷所產，不能充其半，餘皆鑿空取之民間，歲以為常。

translations.literal: The three prefectures of Huizhou, Ningguo, and Guangde annually collected three thousand ingots in tea tax revenue; later it was increased to one hundred eighty thousand ingots. Exhausting all that the mountains and valleys produced could not supply half of it; the remainder was all fabricated and extracted from among the people, and this became an annual routine.
translations.idiomatic: The three prefectures of Huizhou, Ningguo, and Guangde had once yielded three thousand ingots a year in tea tax revenue; the quota was later raised to one hundred eighty thousand. Even the full output of every mountain valley could not meet half the demand—the rest was conjured from thin air and wrung from the people, year after year.

sentences.zh: 時轉運司官聽用鄉里嘩狡，動以犯法誣民，而轉運司得專制有司，凡五品官以下皆杖決，州縣莫敢如何。

translations.literal: At the time the Transport Office officials were allowed to employ local rowdy and cunning men, who frequently framed people on charges of breaking the law. The Transport Office also had unchecked authority over other officials—all officials of fifth rank and below could be beaten and adjudicated at its discretion—and prefectures and counties dared not do anything about it.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Office officials were permitted to hire local bullies and sharpers, who routinely framed commoners for crimes. The office also wielded unchecked power over the regular bureaucracy: any official of fifth rank or below could be beaten and judged at its command, and no prefecture or county dared resist.

sentences.zh: 文原請罷其專司，俾郡縣領之，不報。

translations.literal: Wenyuan requested abolishing this special office and having prefectures and counties take charge of it; no response.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan petitioned to abolish the monopoly office and restore authority to the prefectures and counties; the court did not reply.

sentences.zh: 徽民謝蘭家僮汪姓者死，蘭侄回賂汪族人誣蘭殺之，蘭誣服。

translations.literal: A household servant surnamed Wang in Huizhou resident Xie Lan's household died. Lan's nephew Hui bribed Wang clansmen to accuse Lan of killing him, and Lan confessed under duress.
translations.idiomatic: In Huizhou, a servant surnamed Wang in Xie Lan's household died. Lan's nephew Hui bribed Wang clansmen to accuse Lan of murder, and Lan confessed under torture.

sentences.zh: 文原錄之，得其情，釋蘭而坐回。

translations.literal: Wenyuan interrogated the case, got the true facts, released Lan and punished Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan reviewed the case, uncovered the truth, released Lan, and punished Hui.

sentences.zh: 時久旱不雨，決獄乃雨。

translations.literal: At the time there had been a long drought with no rain; rain fell after he decided the cases.
translations.idiomatic: The region had suffered a long drought; rain fell only after he cleared the miscarriage of justice.

sentences.zh: 至治二年，召為集賢直學士，地震，詔議弭災之道。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi, he was summoned as Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies. There was an earthquake, and an edict ordered discussion of ways to quell the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhizhi he was summoned to serve as Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies. An earthquake struck, and the throne ordered officials to discuss how calamities might be averted.

sentences.zh: 文原請決滯囚，置倉廩河北，儲羨粟以賑饑；

translations.literal: Wenyuan requested releasing long-held prisoners, establishing granaries north of the Yellow River, and storing surplus grain to relieve famine;
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan urged the release of long-detained prisoners, the establishment of granaries north of the Yellow River, and the stockpiling of surplus grain for famine relief;

sentences.zh: 復申前議，請罷榷茶轉運司，又不報。

translations.literal: He again submitted his earlier proposal to abolish the Monopoly Tea Transport Office; again no response.
translations.idiomatic: he also renewed his earlier proposal to abolish the tea monopoly and its transport office—and again received no answer.

sentences.zh: 明年，兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: The next year, he was additionally made Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was additionally appointed Chancellor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 江浙省臣趙簡請開經筵，泰定元年，文原兼經筵官，以疾乞致仕歸。

translations.literal: Zhejiang-Jiangsu provincial official Zhao Jian requested opening the Classic Lecture Hall. In the first year of Taiding, Wenyuan additionally served as a Classic Lecture official; citing illness he requested retirement and returned home.
