translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jian, a Jiang-Zhe provincial official, petitioned to open the Classic Lecture Hall. In the first year of Taiding, Wenyuan served concurrently as a lecture official; citing illness, he requested retirement and returned home.

sentences.zh: 二年，召拜翰林侍講學士，以疾辭。

translations.literal: Second year: summoned and appointed Hanlin Lecturer Academician; declined due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was summoned and appointed Hanlin Lecturing Academician, but declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜嶺北湖南道肅政廉訪使，以疾不赴。

translations.literal: Fourth year: appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Lingbei Hunan Circuit; did not take up the post due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of the Lingbei Hunan Circuit but did not take up the post because of illness.

sentences.zh: 天曆元年卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: First year of Tianli, he died at seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Tianli, at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 文原內嚴而外恕，家貧而行廉。

translations.literal: Wenyuan was stern within but forgiving outwardly, poor at home but upright in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan was strict with himself yet lenient toward others, poor in estate but incorruptible in conduct.

sentences.zh: 初客京師，有一書生病篤，取橐中金，囑文原以歸其親；

translations.literal: When he first sojourned in the capital, there was a scholar who fell gravely ill; he took gold from his purse and entrusted Wenyuan to return it to his parents;
translations.idiomatic: When he first lodged in the capital, a fellow scholar fell gravely ill; he took gold from his purse and entrusted it to Wenyuan to deliver to his parents;

sentences.zh: 既死，而同舍生竊金去，文原買金償死者家，終身不以語人。

translations.literal: After he died, a fellow lodger stole the gold and left. Wenyuan bought gold to compensate the dead man's family, and never told anyone in his lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: After the man died, a roommate stole the gold and fled. Wenyuan bought gold with his own money to repay the dead man's family, and never spoke of it for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 有文集若干卷，內製集若干卷，藏於家。

translations.literal: He had a collected writings of several juan and imperial compositions of several juan, kept at home.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings of several juan and a collection of imperial compositions of several juan, kept in his household.

sentences.zh: 子衍，廕授江浙等處儒學副提舉，未任，卒。

translations.literal: His son Yan received hereditary appointment as Deputy Educational Commissioner of Confucian Studies in Jiang-Zhe and other areas; before taking office, he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan received a hereditary appointment as Deputy Commissioner of Confucian Studies for Jiang-Zhe and other regions, but died before taking office.

sentences.zh: 至順五年，制贈文原江浙行省參知政事，諡文肅。

translations.literal: Fifth year of Zhishun, by decree Wenyuan was posthumously given the title of Vice Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, posthumous name Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhishun, by imperial decree Wenyuan was posthumously made Vice Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wensu.

sentences.zh: 袁桷，字伯長，慶元人，宋同知樞密院事韶之曾孫。

translations.literal: Yuan Jue, style name Bochang, was a native of Qingyuan, great-grandson of Song Vice Director of the Privy Council Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jue, styled Bochang, was a native of Qingyuan and the great-grandson of Shao, who had served the Song as Vice Director of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 為童子時，已著聲。

translations.literal: Even as a child he was already renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was already widely known.

sentences.zh: 部使者舉茂才異等，起為麗澤書院山長。

translations.literal: A regional commissioner recommended him as an outstanding exceptional talent; he was raised to be headmaster of Lizhe Academy.
translations.idiomatic: A regional commissioner recommended him as an outstanding talent of exceptional grade, and he was appointed headmaster of Lizhe Academy.

sentences.zh: 大德初，閻复、程文海、王構薦為翰林國史院檢閱官。

translations.literal: Early in Dade, Yan Fu, Cheng Wenhai, and Wang Gou recommended him as Reviewer of the Hanlin National History Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dade reign, Yan Fu, Cheng Wenhai, and Wang Gou recommended him for appointment as Reviewer of the Hanlin National History Academy.

sentences.zh: 時初建南郊，桷進十議曰：「天無二日，天既不得有二，五帝不得謂之天，作《昊天五帝議》。

translations.literal: When the Southern Suburban Altar was first being built, Jue submitted ten memorials, saying: "Heaven has no second sun; since Heaven cannot have two, the Five Emperors cannot be called Heaven" — he wrote "Memorial on August Heaven and the Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern suburban altar was first under construction, Jue submitted ten memorials, writing: "Heaven has no second sun; if Heaven cannot be duplicated, the Five Emperors cannot be called Heaven" — in his "Memorial on August Heaven and the Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 祭天歲或為九，或為二，作《祭天名數議》。

translations.literal: Heaven sacrifices occur nine times some years and twice in others" — he wrote "Memorial on the Names and Numbers of Heaven Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Some years Heaven is sacrificed to nine times, others only twice" — in his "Memorial on the Names and Numbers of Heaven Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 圜丘不見於《五經》，郊不見於《周官》，作《圜丘非郊議》。

translations.literal: The Round Mound is not found in the Five Classics; the Suburban sacrifice is not found in the Offices of Zhou" — he wrote "Memorial that the Round Mound Is Not the Suburban Sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Round Mound appears nowhere in the Five Classics, nor the Suburban sacrifice in the Offices of Zhou" — in his "Memorial that the Round Mound Is Not the Suburban Sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 后土，社也，作《后土即社議》。

translations.literal: Empress Earth is the soil altar" — he wrote "Memorial that Empress Earth Is the Soil Altar.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Earth is the soil altar" — in his "Memorial that Empress Earth Is the Soil Altar.

sentences.zh: 三歲一郊，非古也，作《祭天無間歲議》。

translations.literal: Suburban sacrifice once every three years is not ancient" — he wrote "Memorial Against Annual Gaps in Heaven Sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: A suburban sacrifice only once every three years is not the ancient way" — in his "Memorial Against Gaps in Annual Heaven Sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 燔柴見於古經，《周官》以禋祀為天，其義各有旨，作《燔柴泰壇議》。

translations.literal: Burning firewood appears in the ancient classics; the Offices of Zhou takes smoke sacrifice as Heaven — each meaning has its point" — he wrote "Memorial on Burning Firewood at the Grand Altar.
translations.idiomatic: Burning firewood appears in the ancient classics, while the Offices of Zhou treats smoke sacrifice as Heaven — each rite has its own intent" — in his "Memorial on Burning Firewood at the Grand Altar.

sentences.zh: 祭天之牛角繭栗，有牲於郊，牛二，合配而言之，增群祀而合祠，非周公之制矣，作《郊不當立從祀議》。

translations.literal: For Heaven sacrifice the ox horn is cocoon-chestnut; there are sacrificial animals at the suburb; two oxen — speaking of combined matching sacrifice, adding group sacrifices and combining temples — is not the system of the Duke of Zhou" — he wrote "Memorial That Suburban Sacrifice Should Not Establish Accompanying Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: For Heaven sacrifice the ox's horn should be small as a silkworm cocoon; a single victim at the suburban rite, two oxen only when speaking of joint matching sacrifice — to add group sacrifices and combine temples is not the Duke of Zhou's system" — in his "Memorial That Suburban Sacrifice Should Not Establish Accompanying Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 郊，質而尊之義也，明堂，文而親之義也，作《郊明堂禮儀異制議》。

translations.literal: Suburban sacrifice is the rite of substance and reverence; the Bright Hall is the rite of culture and intimacy" — he wrote "Memorial on the Separate Institutions of Suburban and Bright Hall Rituals.
translations.idiomatic: The suburban rite embodies substance and reverence; the Bright Hall embodies culture and intimacy" — in his "Memorial on the Separate Institutions of Suburban and Bright Hall Rituals.

sentences.zh: 郊用辛，魯禮也，卜不得常為辛，作《郊非辛日議》。

translations.literal: The suburb uses xin day — that is Lu ritual; divination cannot always be xin" — he wrote "Memorial That Suburban Sacrifice Should Not Be on Xin Days.
translations.idiomatic: Using a xin day for the suburban sacrifice is the rite of Lu; divination cannot always yield xin" — in his "Memorial That Suburban Sacrifice Should Not Be Confined to Xin Days.

sentences.zh: 北郊不見於《三禮》，尊地而遵北郊，鄭玄之說也，作《北郊議》。」

translations.literal: Northern suburb is not found in the Three Rites; honoring earth and observing northern suburb is Zheng Xuan's theory" — he wrote "Memorial on the Northern Suburb."
translations.idiomatic: The northern suburb appears nowhere in the Three Rites; honoring earth through a northern suburban rite is Zheng Xuan's doctrine" — in his "Memorial on the Northern Suburb."

sentences.zh: 禮官推其博，多采用之。

translations.literal: The ritual officials praised his erudition and largely adopted his views.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials admired his learning and largely adopted his proposals.

sentences.zh: 升應奉翰林文字、同知制誥，兼國史院編修官，請購求遼、金、宋三史遺書。

translations.literal: Promoted to Attendant Literary Official of the Hanlin and Concurrent Deputy Director of Edicts, also Compiler of the National History Academy; he requested purchasing surviving books of the Liao, Jin, and Song histories.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Literary Official of the Hanlin and Deputy Director of Edicts, while also serving as Compiler of the National History Academy; he petitioned to purchase surviving books for the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song.

sentences.zh: 歷兩考，遷待制。

translations.literal: After two terms of evaluation, transferred to Drafting Academician.
translations.idiomatic: After two performance reviews he was transferred to Drafting Academician.

sentences.zh: 又再任，拜集賢直學士。

translations.literal: After two more terms, appointed Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: After two further terms he was appointed Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 久之，移疾去官。

translations.literal: After a long time, he resigned citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he resigned from office, citing illness.

sentences.zh: 复仍以直學士召入集賢，未幾，改翰林直學士、知制誥同修國史。

translations.literal: Again summoned as Academician of Gathered Worthies; soon after changed to Hanlin Academician, Director of Edicts, jointly compiling the National History.
translations.idiomatic: He was again summoned as Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies; before long he was transferred to Hanlin Academician, Director of Edicts, and joint compiler of the National History.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: First year of Zhizhi, transferred to Lecturing Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhizhi he was transferred to Lecturing Academician.

sentences.zh: 泰定初，辭歸。

translations.literal: Early Taiding, resigned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiding reign he resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 桷在詞林，朝廷制冊、勳臣碑銘，多出其手。

translations.literal: Jue was in the literary forest; court decrees and meritorious ministers' stele inscriptions mostly came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: While Jue served in the Hanlin, most court decrees and commemorative stele inscriptions for meritorious ministers came from his brush.

sentences.zh: 所著有《易說》、《春秋說》、《清容居士集》。

translations.literal: His works include Exposition on the Changes, Exposition on the Spring and Autumn Annals, and Qingrong Jushi Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included Exposition on the Changes, Exposition on the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the Qingrong Jushi Collection.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: Fourth year of Taiding, he died at sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Taiding, at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈中奉大夫、江浙等處行中書省參知政事、護軍，追封陳留郡公，諡文清。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand Master for Court Audience, Vice Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, Defender of the Army; enfeoffed as Duke of Chenliu; posthumous name Wenqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Court Audience, made Vice Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat and Defender of the Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Chenliu, and given the posthumous name Wenqing.

sentences.zh: 曹元用

translations.literal: Cao Yuanyong
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yuanyong

sentences.zh: 曹元用，字子貞，世居阿城，後徙汶上。

translations.literal: Cao Yuanyong, style name Zizhen, family originally lived in Acheng, later moved to Wenshang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yuanyong, styled Zizhen, came from a family that had long lived in Acheng and later moved to Wenshang.

sentences.zh: 祖義，不仕。

translations.literal: Grandfather Yi did not serve.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yi never entered official service.

sentences.zh: 父宗輔，德清縣主簿。

translations.literal: Father Zongfu was Recorder of Deqing County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zongfu served as Recorder of Deqing County.

sentences.zh: 元用資禀俊爽，幼嗜書，一經目，輒成誦。

translations.literal: Yuanyong's natural endowment was brilliant and unhampered; from youth fond of books; one pass through a text and he could recite it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyong was gifted with a sharp and open nature; from childhood he loved books, and after a single reading he could recite a text from memory.

sentences.zh: 每夜讀書，常達曙不寐。

translations.literal: Each night reading books, often until dawn without sleep.
translations.idiomatic: He read every night, often until dawn without sleeping.

sentences.zh: 父憂其致疾，止之，輒以衣蔽窗默觀之。

translations.literal: Father feared he would fall ill and stopped him; he would cover the window with clothes and read in secret.
translations.idiomatic: His father, fearing illness, forbade him; he would cover the window with clothing and read in secret.

sentences.zh: 始以鎮江路儒學正考滿遊京師。

translations.literal: Initially, having completed his term as Confucian Director of Zhenjiang Circuit, he traveled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He first traveled to the capital after completing his term as Director of Confucian Studies for Zhenjiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 翰林承旨閻复，於四方士少所許可，及見元用，出所為文示之，元用輒指其疵，復大奇之，因薦為翰林國史院編修官。

translations.literal: Hanlin Chancellor Yan Fu rarely approved scholars from all directions; upon seeing Yuanyong, he showed his writings; Yuanyong always pointed out their flaws; Fu greatly marveled and recommended him as Compiler of the National History Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Chancellor Yan Fu rarely praised scholars from anywhere in the realm; when he met Yuanyong and showed him his own writings, Yuanyong at once pointed out their flaws. Fu was deeply impressed and recommended him as Compiler of the Hanlin National History Academy.

sentences.zh: 即論史院僚屬非材，請較試，取其優者用之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he argued the History Academy staff were not competent, requested comparative examination, and use the best.
translations.idiomatic: He then argued that many staff of the History Academy were unqualified, and petitioned for competitive examinations so that only the best might serve.

sentences.zh: 御史臺辟為掾史。

translations.literal: Censorate recruited him as clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate recruited him as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 元用初不習吏事，而見事明決，吏反師之。

translations.literal: Yuanyong initially was not practiced in clerk affairs, but saw matters clearly and decided; clerks in turn took him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyong had no prior training in clerical work, yet saw affairs clearly and decided them firmly; the clerks in turn took him as their teacher.

sentences.zh: 轉中書省右司掾，與清河元明善、濟南張養浩同時號為三俊。

translations.literal: Transferred to Right Branch clerk of the Central Secretariat; together with Yuanshi Yuan Mingshan of Qinghe and Zhang Yanghao of Jinan, simultaneously called the Three Outstanding Men.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to clerk of the Right Branch of the Central Secretariat and, together with Yuan Mingshan of Qinghe and Zhang Yanghao of Jinan, was known at the time as one of the Three Outstanding Men.

sentences.zh: 除應奉翰林文字，遷禮部主事。

translations.literal: Appointed Attendant Literary Official of Hanlin; transferred to Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant Literary Official of the Hanlin and then transferred to Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時累朝皇后既崩者，猶以名稱，而未有諡號。

translations.literal: At the time empresses of successive reigns who had already died still went by personal names, without posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, deceased empresses of successive reigns were still referred to by their personal names, without posthumous honorific titles.

sentences.zh: 元用言：「後為天下母，豈可直稱其名。

translations.literal: Yuanyong said: "Empresses are mothers of the realm — how can one directly call their personal names?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyong said: "An empress is mother of the realm — how can one address her by personal name alone?

sentences.zh: 宜加徽號，以彰懿德。」

translations.literal: One should add honorific titles to display their virtuous merit."
translations.idiomatic: Honorific titles should be added to display their virtuous merit."

sentences.zh: 改尚書省右司都事，轉員外郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to Director of the Right Branch of the Ministry of Revenue and transferred to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Right Branch of the Ministry of Revenue and then promoted to Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 及尚書省罷，退居任城，久之，齊、魯間從學者甚眾。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Revenue was abolished, he retired to Rencheng; after a long time, students in Qi and Lu regions studying under him were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Revenue was abolished, he retired to Rencheng; in time he drew a great many students from Qi and Lu.

sentences.zh: 延祐六年，授太常禮儀院經歷。

translations.literal: Sixth year of Yanyou, appointed Manager of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yanyou he was appointed Manager of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 屬英宗躬修祀事，銳意禮樂，其親祀儀注、鹵簿輿服之制，率所裁定。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Yingzong personally attended to sacrificial affairs and was keen on ritual and music, the protocols for his personal sacrifices, guard of honor, carriage and attire — mostly determined by him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong personally oversaw sacrificial affairs and was devoted to ritual and music; Yuanyong largely determined the protocols for the emperor's personal sacrifices and the regulations for guard of honor, carriages, and ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 初，太廟九室，合饗於一殿，仁宗崩，無室可祔，乃於武宗室前，結彩為次。

translations.literal: Initially the Grand Ancestral Temple had nine chambers, combined feasting in one hall. When Renzong died there was no chamber for enshrinement; they set up a colored silk canopy before Wuzong's chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the Grand Ancestral Temple had nine chambers with combined offerings in one hall. When Renzong died there was no chamber in which to enshrine him, so a colored canopy was erected before Wuzong's chamber as a temporary place.

sentences.zh: 英宗在上京，召禮官集議，元用言：「古者宗廟有寢有室，宜以今室為寢，當更營大殿於前，為十五室。」

translations.literal: Yingzong was at Shangdu and summoned ritual officials to gather and discuss. Yuanyong said: "In antiquity the ancestral temple had sleeping quarters and chambers; the present chambers should serve as sleeping quarters; one should newly build a grand hall in front with fifteen chambers."
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong was at Shangdu and summoned ritual officials to confer. Yuanyong said: "In antiquity the ancestral temple had both sleeping quarters and offering chambers. The present chambers should serve as sleeping quarters, and a new grand hall should be built in front with fifteen chambers."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其議，授翰林待制，升直學士。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his proposal; granted Hanlin Drafting Academician; promoted Academician.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his proposal, appointed him Hanlin Drafting Academician, and promoted him to Academician.

sentences.zh: 至治三年八月，鐵失之變，賊黨赤斤鐵木兒遽至京師，收百司印，趣召兩院學士北上。

translations.literal: August third year of Zhizhi, the Tiezhi Incident — rebel clique Chijin Temur suddenly arrived at the capital, collected seals of all offices, urgently summoned academicians of both academies north.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Zhizhi, during the Tiezhi uprising, the rebel Chijin Temur suddenly reached the capital, seized the seals of every office, and urgently summoned the academicians of both Hanlin academies northward.

sentences.zh: 元用獨不行，曰：「此非常之變，吾寧死，不可曲從也。」

translations.literal: Yuanyong alone did not go, saying: "This is an extraordinary upheaval; I would rather die than bow to it."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyong alone refused to go, saying: "This is no ordinary crisis; I would rather die than submit to it."

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊果敗，人皆稱其有先見之明。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels were indeed defeated; everyone praised his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels were indeed defeated, and all praised his foresight.

sentences.zh: 泰定二年，授太子贊善，轉禮部尚書，兼經筵官，及大朝會，為糾儀官，申卷班之令。

translations.literal: Second year of Taiding, appointed Tutor to the Crown Prince; transferred Minister of Rites; also Classic Lecture official. At great court assemblies he served as ritual correction official, enforcing the order to withdraw in files.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiding he was appointed Tutor to the Crown Prince, then transferred to Minister of Rites and also served as a Classic Lecture official. At great court assemblies he served as ritual correction officer, enforcing the order to withdraw in ranks.

sentences.zh: 俾以序退，無爭門而出之擾。

translations.literal: So they withdrew in sequence, without the disorder of crowding the gates to exit.
translations.idiomatic: Officials withdrew in proper order, without the disorder of crowding the gates.

sentences.zh: 又謂太醫、儀鳳、教坊等官，不當序正班，當自為一列，後皆行之。

translations.literal: He also said officials of the Imperial Medical Service, Ceremonial Music Service, and Training Bureau should not be ranked in the regular court order but should form their own column; later all were implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that officials of the Imperial Medical Service, Ceremonial Music Office, and Training Bureau should not stand in the regular court ranks but in a separate column; this was later adopted.

sentences.zh: 時宰執有欲罷科舉法者，元用以為「國家文治，正在於此，胡可罷也」。

translations.literal: At the time chief ministers wished to abolish the examination system; Yuanyong said "The state's literary governance lies precisely in this — how can it be abolished?"
translations.idiomatic: Some chief ministers at the time wished to abolish the civil service examinations; Yuanyong declared that "the state's civil governance rests precisely on this — how can it be abolished?"

sentences.zh: 又有欲損太廟四時之享、止存冬祭者，元用謂：「禴祠嘗烝，四時之享，不可闕一，乃經禮之大者，其可惜費而廢禮乎！」

translations.literal: There were also those who wished to reduce the four seasonal offerings at the Grand Temple, keeping only winter sacrifice. Yuanyong said: "Yu, ci, chang, and zheng — the four seasonal offerings — not one may be omitted; these are the greatest of canonical ritual. Can one regret the expense and discard ritual?"
translations.idiomatic: Others proposed reducing the Grand Temple's four seasonal offerings to winter sacrifice alone. Yuanyong said: "The spring, summer, autumn, and winter offerings — not one of the four seasonal sacrifices may be omitted; they are among the greatest rites of the classics. Can expense justify abandoning ritual?"

sentences.zh: 三年夏，帝以日食、地震、星變，詔議所以弭災者，元用謂：「應天以實不以文，修德明政，應天之實也。

translations.literal: Third year summer, the emperor because of solar eclipse, earthquake, and star anomalies ordered discussion of how to quell calamities. Yuanyong said: "Responding to Heaven requires substance not ornament; cultivating virtue and clarifying governance is the substance of responding to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year, after a solar eclipse, earthquakes, and celestial anomalies, the emperor ordered discussion of how to avert calamity. Yuanyong said: "Heaven is answered with substance, not show; cultivating virtue and governing well is the substance of answering Heaven.

sentences.zh: 宜撙浮費，節財用，選守令，卹貧民，嚴禋祀，汰佛事，止造作以紓民力，慎賞罰以示勸懲。」

translations.literal: One should curtail extravagant expenses, economize finances, select prefects and magistrates, relieve the poor, strictly perform smoke sacrifices, cut Buddhist affairs, halt construction to ease people's labor, and be careful with rewards and punishments to show encouragement and admonition."
translations.idiomatic: Extravagant spending should be cut, finances conserved, prefects and magistrates carefully chosen, the poor relieved, sacrificial rites strictly observed, Buddhist ceremonies reduced, construction halted to ease the people's burden, and rewards and punishments applied with care to encourage virtue and warn against wrong."

sentences.zh: 皆切中時弊。

translations.literal: All struck at the ills of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Every proposal struck directly at the abuses of the age.

sentences.zh: 又論科舉取士之法，當革冒濫，嚴考核，俾得真才之用。

translations.literal: Also discussed the examination method for selecting scholars — should reform false inflation, strictly examine, so true talent could be employed.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the examination system for selecting officials should be reformed to eliminate abuse, tighten evaluation, and ensure that true talent was employed.

sentences.zh: 議上，朝廷咸是之。

translations.literal: When the memorials went up, the court all approved.
translations.idiomatic: When his memorials were submitted, the court approved them all.

sentences.zh: 拜中奉大夫、翰林侍講學士，兼經筵官，預修仁宗、英宗兩朝實錄。

translations.literal: Appointed Grand Master for Court Audience, Hanlin Lecturing Academician, also Classic Lecture official; participated in compiling Veritable Records of Renzong and Yingzong reigns.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Master for Court Audience and Hanlin Lecturing Academician, also serving as a Classic Lecture official, and participated in compiling the Veritable Records of the Renzong and Yingzong reigns.

sentences.zh: 又奉旨纂集甲令為《通制》，譯唐《貞觀政要》為國語。

translations.literal: Also received decree to compile ordinances into Comprehensive Regulations; translated Tang Zhenguan Political Essentials into the national language.
translations.idiomatic: He also received orders to compile statutes into the Comprehensive Regulations and to translate the Tang Zhenguan Political Essentials into the national language.

sentences.zh: 書成，皆行於時。

translations.literal: When the books were completed, all were implemented at the time.
translations.idiomatic: When the works were completed, all were put into effect.

sentences.zh: 凡大制誥，率元用所草。

translations.literal: For great edicts, mostly drafted by Yuanyong.
translations.idiomatic: Major imperial edicts were mostly drafted by Yuanyong.

sentences.zh: 文宗時，草寬卹之詔，帝覽而善之，賜金織文錦。

translations.literal: During Wenzong's time, he drafted the amnesty edict for relief; the emperor read it and approved, bestowing gold-woven brocade.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Wenzong he drafted an edict granting relief and clemency; the emperor read it with approval and bestowed gold-woven brocade.

sentences.zh: 天曆二年，代祀曲阜孔子廟。

translations.literal: Second year of Tianli, deputized to sacrifice at Confucius Temple in Qufu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianli he was deputized to perform sacrifice at the Confucius Temple in Qufu.

sentences.zh: 還，以司寇像及代祀記獻，帝甚喜。

translations.literal: On return, presented portrait of the Minister of Crime and record of deputized sacrifice; emperor was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he presented a portrait of Confucius as Minister of Crime and a record of the deputized sacrifice; the emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 值太禧宗禋院副使缺，中書奏以元用為之，帝不允曰：「此人翰林中所不可無者，將大用之矣。」

translations.literal: When Vice Commissioner of the Court of Imperial Ancestor Sacrifices was vacant, Central Secretariat memorialized Yuanyong for the post; emperor did not approve, saying: "This man is indispensable in the Hanlin; he will be greatly employed."
translations.idiomatic: When the post of Vice Commissioner of the Court of Imperial Ancestor Sacrifices fell vacant, the Central Secretariat memorialized to appoint Yuanyong; the emperor refused, saying: "This man is indispensable to the Hanlin; greater appointments await him."

sentences.zh: 會卒，帝嗟悼久之，謂侍臣曰：「曹子貞盡忠宣力，今亡矣，可賜賻鈔五千緡。」

translations.literal: As it happened he died; emperor sighed in mourning for a long time, telling attendants: "Cao Zizhen served loyally with all his strength; now he is gone. Bestow five thousand strings of burial money."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yuanyong died. The emperor mourned him at length and told his attendants: "Cao Zizhen served loyally with all his strength; now he is gone. Grant five thousand strings of burial money."

sentences.zh: 贈政奉大夫、江浙等處行中書省參知政事、護軍，追封東平郡公，諡文獻。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Zhengfeng Grand Master, Vice Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, Defender of the Army; enfeoffed as Duke of Dongping; posthumous name Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Advancing Governance, made Vice Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat and Defender of the Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Dongping, and given the posthumous name Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 詩文四十卷，號《超然集》。

translations.literal: Poetry and prose forty juan, titled Chaoran Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose, forty juan in all, were collected under the title Chaoran Collection.

sentences.zh: 二子：偉，儀。

translations.literal: Two sons: Wei and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Wei and Yi.

sentences.zh: 齊履謙

translations.literal: Qi Luqian
translations.idiomatic: Qi Luqian

sentences.zh: 齊履謙，字伯恆，父義，善算術。

translations.literal: Qi Luqian, style name Boheng, father Yi was skilled in calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Luqian, styled Boheng, was the son of Yi, who was skilled in mathematics.

sentences.zh: 履謙生六歲，從父至京師；

translations.literal: Luqian at six sui followed his father to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Luqian was six when he accompanied his father to the capital;

sentences.zh: 七歲讀書，一過即能記憶；

translations.literal: At seven he began reading books; one pass and he could memorize;
translations.idiomatic: at seven he began to read, and after a single pass he could memorize what he had read;

sentences.zh: 年十一，教以推步星曆，盡曉其法；

translations.literal: At eleven, taught astrological calendrical computation; fully understood the methods;
translations.idiomatic: at eleven he was taught astronomical calendrical calculation and mastered the methods entirely;

sentences.zh: 十三，從師，聞聖賢之學。

translations.literal: At thirteen, followed a teacher, heard the learning of sages and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he became a pupil and began to study the learning of the sages.

sentences.zh: 自是以窮理為務，非洙、泗、伊、洛之書不讀。

translations.literal: From this he took penetrating principle as his task; only books of Zhu, Si, Yi, and Luo he read.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he devoted himself to investigating principle, and would read nothing except the works of the Confucian and Neo-Confucian masters associated with Zhou, Si, Yi, and Luo.

sentences.zh: 至元十六年，初立太史局，改治新歷，履謙補星曆生。

translations.literal: Sixteenth year of Zhiyuan, first established Grand Astrologer Bureau, reformed and compiled new calendar; Luqian supplemented as star-calendar student.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan, when the Grand Astrologer Bureau was first established to compile a new calendar, Luqian was appointed a student of star-calendars.

sentences.zh: 同輩皆司天台官子，太史王恂問以算數，莫能對，履謙獨隨問隨答，恂大奇之。

translations.literal: Peers were all sons of Bureau of Astronomy officials; Grand Astrologer Wang Xun questioned them on calculation; none could answer; Luqian alone answered as asked; Xun greatly marveled.
translations.idiomatic: His peers were all sons of Bureau of Astronomy officials. When Grand Astrologer Wang Xun questioned them on mathematics, none could answer, but Luqian replied to each question as it came, and Xun was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 新歷既成，复預修《曆經》、《曆議》。

translations.literal: New calendar already completed, again participated in compiling Calendar Classic and Calendar Discourse.
translations.idiomatic: After the new calendar was completed, he also took part in compiling the Calendar Classic and Calendar Discourse.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，授星曆教授。

translations.literal: Twenty-ninth year, granted Instructor in Star-Calendars.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed Instructor in Star-Calendars.

sentences.zh: 都城刻漏，舊以木為之，其形如碑，故名碑漏，內設曲筒，鑄銅為丸，自碑首轉行而下，鳴鐃以為節，其漏經久廢壞，晨昏失度。

translations.literal: Capital clepsydra, formerly made of wood; its form like a stele, hence named stele clepsydra; inside set curved tubes, cast copper as balls, from stele top turning and descending, sounding cymbals as beats; the clepsydra long abandoned and broken, dawn and dusk lost measure.
translations.idiomatic: The capital clepsydra had formerly been made of wood. Shaped like a stele, it was called the stele clepsydra. Inside were curved tubes and copper balls cast to roll down from the top of the stele, while cymbals sounded the beats. The device had long fallen into disrepair, and the hours of dawn and dusk were no longer kept correctly.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，中書俾履謙視之，因見刻漏旁有宋舊銅壺四，於是按圖考定蓮花、寶山等漏制，命工改作，又請重建鼓樓，增置更鼓並守漏卒，當時遵用之。

translations.literal: First year of Dade, Secretariat dispatched Luqian to inspect it; seeing beside the clepsydra four old Song copper vessels; thereupon according to drawings verified Lotus, Baoshan, and other clepsydra designs, ordered craftsmen to remake; also requested rebuilding drum tower, adding watch drums and clepsydra guards; at the time adopted and used.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dade the Secretariat sent Luqian to inspect it. He noticed four old Song copper clepsydra vessels beside the stele clepsydra, consulted the drawings to verify the Lotus, Baoshan, and other designs, and ordered craftsmen to remake them. He also requested rebuilding the drum tower and adding watch drums and clepsydra guards, all of which was then put into use.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷保章正，始專歷官之政。

translations.literal: Second year, transferred to Director of the Bureau of Astronomy; began exclusively managing calendrical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to Director of the Bureau of Astronomy and began to devote himself entirely to calendrical administration.

sentences.zh: 三年八月朔，時加巳，依歷，日蝕二分有奇，至其時，不蝕，眾皆懼，履謙曰：「當蝕不蝕，在古有之，矧時近午，陽盛陰微，宜當蝕不蝕。」

translations.literal: Third year eighth month new moon, hour added si; according to calendar, solar eclipse two-tenths odd; when the time came, no eclipse; all feared; Luqian said: "When eclipse expected, no eclipse — in antiquity this has occurred; moreover the time is near noon, yang flourishing yin faint — fitting that expected eclipse does not eclipse."
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eighth month of the third year, at the si hour, the calendar predicted a solar eclipse of slightly more than two-tenths. When the moment came there was no eclipse, and all were alarmed. Luqian said, "An expected eclipse that fails to occur has happened in antiquity. Moreover the time was near noon, when yang flourishes and yin is faint — it was fitting that the eclipse should not occur."

sentences.zh: 遂考唐開元以來當蝕不蝕者凡十事以聞。

translations.literal: Thereupon researched from Tang Kaiyuan onward cases of expected eclipse not eclipsing, ten instances in all, and reported.
translations.idiomatic: He then researched ten instances since the Tang Kaiyuan era in which an expected eclipse had failed to occur and reported them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 六年六月朔，時加戌，依歷，日蝕五十七秒。

translations.literal: Sixth year sixth month new moon, hour added xu; according to calendar, solar eclipse fifty-seven seconds.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the sixth month of the sixth year, at the xu hour, the calendar predicted a solar eclipse of fifty-seven seconds.

sentences.zh: 眾以涉交既淺，且復近濁，欲匿不報。

translations.literal: The group, because crossing already shallow, and again near turbidity, wished to conceal and not report.
translations.idiomatic: The others, thinking the lunar crossing too shallow and the sun too near the horizon haze, wished to suppress the prediction and not report it.

sentences.zh: 履謙曰：「吾所掌者，常數也，其食與否，則係於天。」

translations.literal: Luqian said: "What I manage is the regular calculation; whether it eclipses or not depends on Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Luqian said, "What I am responsible for is the regular calculation; whether an eclipse occurs depends on Heaven."

sentences.zh: 獨以狀聞。

translations.literal: Alone reported by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He alone reported it by memorial.

sentences.zh: 及其時，果食。

translations.literal: When the time came, indeed eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: When the time came, the eclipse occurred as predicted.

sentences.zh: 眾嘗爭沒日不能決，履謙曰：「氣本十五日，而間有十六日者，餘分之積也。

translations.literal: The group once disputed hidden day and could not decide; Luqian said: "Qi originally fifteen days, yet sometimes sixteen days — accumulation of fractional days.
translations.idiomatic: The group once disputed the reckoning of hidden days and could not settle the matter. Luqian said, "A qi normally has fifteen days, yet sometimes there are sixteen — this is the accumulation of fractional days.

sentences.zh: 故曆法以所積之日，命為沒日，不出本氣者為是。」

translations.literal: Therefore calendrical method takes accumulated days and names them hidden day; not exceeding the original qi is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Calendrical method therefore names the accumulated days as the hidden day; so long as one does not exceed the original qi, the reckoning is correct."

sentences.zh: 眾服其議。

translations.literal: The group submitted to his reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: The group accepted his reasoning.

sentences.zh: 七年八月戊申夜，地大震，詔問致災之由及弭災之道，履謙按《春秋》言：「地為陰而主靜，妻道、臣道、子道也，三者失其道，則地為之弗寧。

translations.literal: Seventh year eighth month wushen night, great earthquake; edict asked cause of disaster and way to quell disaster; Luqian cited Spring and Autumn Annals, saying: "Earth is yin and presides over stillness — way of wife, minister, and child; when these three lose their way, earth is disturbed for them.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of wushen in the eighth month of the seventh year a great earthquake struck. An edict asked the cause of the calamity and the means of quelling it. Luqian cited the Spring and Autumn Annals, saying, "Earth is yin and presides over stillness — the way of wife, minister, and child. When these three lose their proper course, the earth is disturbed.

sentences.zh: 弭之之道，大臣當反躬責己，去專制之威，以答天變，不可徒為禳禱也。」

translations.literal: Way to quell it: great ministers should turn inward and blame themselves, remove autocratic severity, to answer Heaven's warning — must not merely perform exorcistic prayers."
translations.idiomatic: The way to quell it is for great ministers to turn inward and blame themselves, set aside autocratic severity, and answer Heaven's warning — not merely to perform exorcistic prayers."

sentences.zh: 時成宗寢疾，宰臣有專威福者，故履謙言及之。

translations.literal: At the time Chengzong seriously ill; among chief ministers one monopolized power and favor — hence Luqian's remark.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Chengzong lay gravely ill, and among the chief ministers was one who monopolized power and favor — hence Luqian's remark.

sentences.zh: 九年冬，始立南郊，祀昊天上帝，履謙攝司天臺官。

translations.literal: Ninth year winter, first established Southern Suburban Altar, sacrificed to August Heaven; Luqian acted as Bureau of Astronomy officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the ninth year the Southern Suburban Altar was first established to sacrifice to August Heaven, and Luqian served as acting Bureau of Astronomy officer.

sentences.zh: 舊制，享祀，司天雖掌時刻，無鐘鼓更漏，往往至旦始行事。

translations.literal: Old system: at sacrifices, though Bureau of Astronomy managed hours, no bell-drums or watch clepsydra; often until dawn before performing rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, although the Bureau of Astronomy managed the hours at sacrifices, there were no bell-drums or watch clepsydra, and ceremonies often did not begin until dawn.

sentences.zh: 履謙白宰執，請用鐘鼓更漏，俾早晏有節，從之。

translations.literal: Luqian informed chief executives, requested using bell-drums and watch clepsydra, so early and late would have measure; agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Luqian informed the chief executives and requested bell-drums and a watch clepsydra so that early and late would be properly measured; they agreed.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，太常請修社稷壇，及浚太廟庭中井。

translations.literal: Second year of Zhide, Court of Imperial Sacrifices requested repairing altar of soil and grain and dredging well in Grand Ancestral Temple courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhide the Court of Imperial Sacrifices requested repairs to the altar of soil and grain and dredging of the well in the Grand Ancestral Temple courtyard.

sentences.zh: 或以歲君所直，欲止其役，履謙曰：「國家以四海為家，歲君豈專在是！」

translations.literal: Some, citing year's astral patron's position, wished to halt the labor; Luqian said: "State takes Four Seas as home — how could year's patron be confined to this alone!"
translations.idiomatic: Some, citing the year's astral patron, wished to halt the work. Luqian said, "The state takes all within the Four Seas as its home — how could the year's patron be confined to this place alone!"

sentences.zh: 三年，升授時郎秋官正，兼領冬官正事。

translations.literal: Third year, promoted to Autumn Bureau Director of Directorate of Astronomy, concurrently managing Winter Bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Autumn Bureau Director of the Directorate of Astronomy, concurrently managing Winter Bureau affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年，仁宗即位，嘉尚儒術。

translations.literal: Fourth year, Renzong acceded, prized Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Renzong acceded to the throne and prized Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 台臣言履謙有學行，可教國學子弟，擢國子監丞，改授奉直大夫、國子司業，與吳澄並命，時號得人。

translations.literal: Censorate officials said Luqian had learning and conduct, could teach Imperial Academy students; raised to Deputy Director of National University, changed to Granting Directness Grand Master and Vice Chancellor of National University, together with Wu Cheng appointed; at the time called successful selection of men.
translations.idiomatic: Censorate officials reported that Luqian possessed learning and conduct fit to instruct Imperial Academy students. He was promoted to Deputy Director of the National University, then appointed Granting Directness Grand Master and Vice Chancellor of the National University together with Wu Cheng — at the time regarded as an excellent choice of men.

sentences.zh: 每五鼓入學，風雨寒暑，未嘗少怠，其教養有法，諸生皆畏服。

translations.literal: Every fifth watch entered academy; wind, rain, cold, heat — never slightly slackened; teaching and nurture had method; students all feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Every day at the fifth watch he entered the academy. Through wind, rain, cold, and heat he never slackened. His teaching and nurture were methodical, and the students all feared and respected him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復以履謙僉太史院事。

translations.literal: Before long, again made Luqian Concurrent Administrator of Astronomical Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Luqian was again appointed Concurrent Administrator of the Astronomical Academy.

sentences.zh: 皇慶二年春，彗星出東井。

translations.literal: Second year of Huangqing spring, comet appeared at Well constellation.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Huangqing a comet appeared in the Well constellation.

sentences.zh: 履謙奏宜增修善政以答天意，因陳時務八事。

translations.literal: Luqian memorialized that good governance should be increased to answer Heaven's intent; thereupon set forth eight matters of current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Luqian memorialized that good governance should be strengthened to answer Heaven's intent, and set forth eight matters of current affairs.

sentences.zh: 仁宗為之動容，顧宰臣命速行之。

translations.literal: Renzong was moved; turning to chief ministers ordered speedily carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong was visibly moved and, turning to the chief ministers, ordered the proposals carried out at once.

sentences.zh: 自履謙去國學，吳澄亦移病歸，學制稍為之廢。

translations.literal: Since Luqian left Imperial Academy, Wu Cheng also took leave on illness and returned; academy system somewhat neglected for it.
translations.idiomatic: After Luqian left the Imperial Academy, Wu Cheng also took leave on grounds of illness and returned home, and the academy system was somewhat neglected.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，詔擇善教者，於是復以履謙為國子司業。

translations.literal: First year of Yanyou, edict selected good teachers; thereupon again made Luqian Vice Chancellor of National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanyou an edict called for selecting good teachers, and Luqian was again appointed Vice Chancellor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 履謙律己益嚴，教道益張，每齋置伴讀一人為長，雖助教闕員，而諸生講授不絕。

translations.literal: Luqian disciplined himself ever stricter, teaching way ever broader; each dormitory placed one reading companion as head; though assistant instructor posts vacant, students' lectures never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Luqian disciplined himself ever more strictly and spread his teaching ever more broadly. In each dormitory he placed one reading companion as head, and though assistant instructor posts stood vacant, the students' lectures never ceased.

sentences.zh: 時初命國子生歲貢六人，以入學先後為次第，履謙曰：「不考其業，何以興善而得人！」

translations.literal: At the time first ordered six National University students for annual tribute, by order of enrollment as sequence; Luqian said: "Not examining their achievement — how cultivate good and obtain men!"
translations.idiomatic: At the time six National University students were first appointed for annual tribute, ranked simply by order of enrollment. Luqian said, "If their achievement is not examined, how can good be cultivated and worthy men obtained!"

sentences.zh: 乃酌舊制，立昇齋、積分等法：每季考其學行，以次遞升，既升上齋，又必逾再歲，始與私試；

translations.literal: Thereupon drew on old regulations, established methods of rising dormitories and accumulating points: each season examined learning and conduct, promoted in sequence; once risen to upper dormitory, must pass two more years before private examinations;
translations.idiomatic: He then drew on old regulations and established methods of rising dormitories and accumulating points: each season students' learning and conduct were examined for successive promotion; once promoted to the upper dormitory they had to pass two more years before taking private examinations;

sentences.zh: 孟月仲月試經疑經義，季月試古賦詔誥章表策，蒙古、色目試明經策問；

translations.literal: First and second months of season tested difficult passages and meaning in classics; third month tested ancient-style prose, edicts, memorials, formal documents, and policy essays; Mongols and Semuren tested classics-and-meaning policy questions;
translations.idiomatic: In the first and second months of each season they were tested on difficult passages and the meaning of the classics; in the third month on ancient-style prose, edicts, memorials, formal documents, and policy essays; Mongols and Semuren on classics-and-meaning policy questions;

sentences.zh: 辭理俱優者一分，辭平理優者為半分，歲終積至八分者充高等，以四十人為額；

translations.literal: Both diction and reasoning excellent — one point; diction average, reasoning excellent — half point; at year's end accumulated to eight points ranked high, quota forty persons;
translations.idiomatic: Those excellent in both diction and reasoning received one point; those average in diction but excellent in reasoning received half a point; at year's end those who accumulated eight points ranked high, with a quota of forty;

sentences.zh: 然後集賢、禮部定其藝業及格者六人，以充歲貢；

translations.literal: Then Hanlin Academy and Ministry of Rites determined those whose arts qualified — six to fill annual tribute;
translations.idiomatic: Then the Hanlin Academy and Ministry of Rites determined those whose arts qualified, and six were chosen to fill the annual tribute;

sentences.zh: 三年不通一經，及在學不滿一歲者，並黜之。

translations.literal: Three years without mastering one classic, and those in academy less than one year — all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who after three years had not mastered one classic, and those who had been in the academy less than one year, were all dismissed.

sentences.zh: 帝從其議，自是人人勵志，多文學之士。

translations.literal: Emperor accepted his proposal; from then all exerted themselves; many men of letters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his proposal, and from then on everyone exerted themselves, producing many men of letters.

sentences.zh: 五年，出為濱州知州，丁母憂，不果行。

translations.literal: Fifth year, sent out as Prefect of Binzhou; mother died and mourned; did not take up post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed Prefect of Binzhou, but his mother died and he entered mourning, so he never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，拜太史院使。

translations.literal: First year of Zhizhi, appointed Director of Astronomical Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhizhi he was appointed Director of the Astronomical Academy.

sentences.zh: 泰定二年九月，以本官奉使宣撫江西、福建，黜罷官吏之貪污者四百餘人，蠲免括地虛加糧數万石，州縣以先賢子孫充房夫諸役者悉罷遣之。

translations.literal: Second year of Taiding ninth month, in original capacity sent as Pacification Commissioner to Jiangxi and Fujian; dismissed corrupt officials more than four hundred; remitted falsely levied land-assessment grain tens of thousands of shi; in prefectures and counties those made corvée laborers as descendants of former sages — all released and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year of Taiding, in his existing capacity he was sent as Pacification Commissioner to Jiangxi and Fujian. He dismissed more than four hundred corrupt officials, remitted tens of thousands of shi of falsely levied land-assessment grain, and in prefectures and counties released all those forced to serve as corvée laborers because they were descendants of former sages.

sentences.zh: 福建憲司職田，每畝歲輸米三石，民不勝苦。

translations.literal: Fujian Censorate official fields, each mu yearly delivered three shi of rice; people could not bear the hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The Fujian Censorate's official fields required three shi of rice per mu each year, a burden the people could not bear.

sentences.zh: 履謙命準令輸之，由是召怨，及還京，憲司果誣以他事。

translations.literal: Luqian ordered payment according to statute; thereby incurred resentment; when returned to capital, Censorate indeed falsely accused on other matters.
translations.idiomatic: Luqian ordered payment according to statute, thereby incurring resentment. When he returned to the capital, the Censorate falsely accused him on other grounds.

sentences.zh: 未幾，誣履謙者皆坐事免，履謙始得直，復為太史院使。

translations.literal: Before long, those who falsely accused Luqian all dismissed for offenses; Luqian finally cleared, again Director of Astronomical Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long those who had falsely accused Luqian were all dismissed for offenses; Luqian was finally cleared and restored as Director of the Astronomical Academy.

sentences.zh: 天曆二年九月卒。

translations.literal: Second year of Tianli ninth month died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of the second year of Tianli.

sentences.zh: 履謙篤學勤苦，家貧無書。

translations.literal: Luqian deeply devoted to learning, diligent in hardship; family poor, no books.
translations.idiomatic: Luqian was deeply devoted to learning and endured hardship in his studies; his family was poor and owned no books.

sentences.zh: 及為星曆生，在太史局，會秘書監輦亡宋故書，留置本院，因晝夜諷誦，深究自得，故其學博洽精通，自六經、諸史、天文、地理、禮樂、律曆，下至陰陽五行、醫藥、卜筮，無不淹貫，尤精經籍。

translations.literal: When star-calendar student, in Grand Astrologer Bureau, met Secretariat transporting lost Song old books, retained in this bureau; therefore day and night recited, deeply investigated and obtained for himself; hence his learning broad, thorough, and penetrating — from Six Classics, various histories, astronomy, geography, ritual, music, pitch and calendar, down to yin-yang five phases, medicine, divination — none not thoroughly mastered; especially refined in classics.
translations.idiomatic: When he became a star-calendar student at the Grand Astrologer Bureau, the Secretariat happened to transport old Song books and left them at the bureau. He recited them day and night, investigating deeply until he mastered them for himself. His learning became broad, thorough, and penetrating — from the Six Classics and various histories through astronomy, geography, ritual, music, pitch pipes, and calendrics, down to yin-yang, the five phases, medicine, and divination, nothing escaped his grasp — and he was especially refined in the classics.

sentences.zh: 著《大學四傳小注》一卷，《中庸章句續解》一卷，《論語言仁通旨》二卷，《書傳詳說》一卷，《易繫辭旨略》二卷，《易本說》四卷，《春秋諸國統紀》六卷。

translations.literal: Authored Small Commentary on the Four Commentaries of the Great Learning, one juan; Continued Explication of the Doctrine of the Mean, one juan; Comprehensive Purpose of Ren in the Analects, two juan; Detailed Explanation of the Book of Documents, one juan; Essential Outline of the Appended Remarks on the Changes, two juan; Original Explanation of the Changes, four juan; Comprehensive Chronicle of the States in the Spring and Autumn, six juan.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Small Commentary on the Four Commentaries of the Great Learning, one juan; Continued Explication of the Doctrine of the Mean, one juan; Comprehensive Purpose of Ren in the Analects, two juan; Detailed Explanation of the Book of Documents, one juan; Essential Outline of the Appended Remarks on the Changes, two juan; Original Explanation of the Changes, four juan; and Comprehensive Chronicle of the States in the Spring and Autumn, six juan.

sentences.zh: 以皇極之名見於《洪範》，皇極之數始於邵氏《經世書》，數非極也，特寓其數極耳，著《經世書入式》一卷；

translations.literal: Supreme Ultimate name appears in Hong Fan; Supreme Ultimate numbers begin in Shao's Classic of the Ages; numbers are not the Ultimate — merely embodying numbers at the Ultimate; authored Introduction to the Classic of the Ages, one juan;
translations.idiomatic: The name Supreme Ultimate appears in the Hong Fan; the numbers of the Supreme Ultimate begin in Shao Yong's Classic of the Ages. Numbers are not the Ultimate itself — they merely embody the Ultimate in number — and he authored Introduction to the Classic of the Ages, one juan;

sentences.zh: 《經世書》有內、外篇，內篇則因極而明數，外篇則由數而會極，著《外篇微旨》一卷。

translations.literal: Classic of the Ages has inner and outer sections; inner section proceeds from the Ultimate to clarify numbers; outer section proceeds from numbers to converge on the Ultimate; authored Subtle Purpose of the Outer Section, one juan.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of the Ages has inner and outer sections: the inner section proceeds from the Ultimate to clarify numbers, and the outer section proceeds from numbers to converge on the Ultimate. He authored Subtle Purpose of the Outer Section, one juan.

sentences.zh: 《授時曆》行五十年，未嘗推考，履謙日測晷景，並晨昏五星宿度，自至治三年冬至至泰定二年夏至，天道加時真數，各減見行曆書二刻，著《二至晷景考》二卷。

translations.literal: Season-Granting Calendar in use fifty years, never examined by calculation; Luqian daily measured gnomon shadow, together with dawn and dusk five planets and lodge degrees; from third year of Zhizhi winter solstice to second year of Taiding summer solstice, true numbers of celestial motion added to the hours — each reduced current calendar by two quarters; authored Examination of Gnomon Shadows at the Two Solstices, two juan.
translations.idiomatic: The Season-Granting Calendar had been in use for fifty years without recalculation. Luqian measured gnomon shadows daily, together with the positions of the five planets and lodge degrees at dawn and dusk. From the winter solstice of the third year of Zhizhi to the summer solstice of the second year of Taiding, he determined the true numbers of celestial motion added to the hours, each reducing the current calendar by two quarters, and authored Examination of Gnomon Shadows at the Two Solstices, two juan.

sentences.zh: 《授時曆》雖有經、串，而經以著定法，串以紀成數，然求其法之所以然、數之所從出，則略而不載，作《經串演撰八法》一卷。

translations.literal: Season-Granting Calendar though has main text and auxiliary strings — main text sets fixed methods, auxiliary strings record completed numbers — yet seeking why the methods are so and whence the numbers arise, it omits and does not record; composed Eight Methods of Elaborating the Main Text and Auxiliary Strings, one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Although the Season-Granting Calendar has a main text and auxiliary strings — the main text setting fixed methods and the auxiliary strings recording completed numbers — it omits the reasons the methods are as they are and the sources from which the numbers arise. He composed Eight Methods of Elaborating the Main Text and Auxiliary Strings, one juan.

sentences.zh: 元立國百有餘年，而郊廟之樂，沿襲宋、金，未有能正之者。

translations.literal: Yuan established state more than a hundred years; suburban and temple music followed Song and Jin; none able to correct it.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan had been established for more than a hundred years, yet the music of the suburban and temple sacrifices still followed Song and Jin and no one had been able to correct it.

sentences.zh: 履謙謂樂本於律，律本於氣，而氣候之法，具載前史，可擇僻地為密室，取金門之竹及河內葭莩候之，上可以正雅樂、薦郊廟、和神人，下可以同度量、平物貨、厚風俗。

translations.literal: Luqian said music rooted in pitch pipes, pitch pipes rooted in qi; methods of seasonal qi fully recorded in former histories; could select secluded place for sealed chamber, take Jin Gate bamboo and Hedong reed-foetus and observe them — above could correct elegant music, present at suburban and temple sacrifices, harmonize spirits and men; below could unify measures, level goods and currency, enrich customs.
translations.idiomatic: Luqian held that music is rooted in pitch pipes and pitch pipes in qi, and that the methods for observing seasonal qi are fully recorded in earlier histories. One could select a secluded place for a sealed chamber, take bamboo from Jin Gate and reed-foetus from Hedong, and observe them — thereby correcting elegant music above, presenting it at suburban and temple sacrifices, and harmonizing spirits and men, and below unifying measures, leveling goods and currency, and enriching customs.

sentences.zh: 列其事上之。

translations.literal: Listed the matter and submitted upward.
translations.idiomatic: He set forth the proposal and submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 又得黑石古律管一，長尺有八寸，外方，內為圓空，中有隔，隔中有小竅，蓋以通氣；

translations.literal: Also obtained one ancient black-stone pitch pipe, length one chi eight cun; outer square, inner circular hollow; inside a partition; within the partition a small aperture — presumably to vent qi;
translations.idiomatic: He also obtained an ancient black-stone pitch pipe one chi and eight cun long, square on the outside and hollow and round within, with a partition inside and a small aperture in the partition, presumably to vent the qi;

sentences.zh: 隔上九寸，其空均直，約徑三分，以應黃鐘之數；

translations.literal: Above the partition nine cun; its hollow uniform and straight, approximately three fen in diameter, to correspond to yellow bell's number;
translations.idiomatic: Above the partition was nine cun; its hollow was uniform and straight, approximately three fen in diameter, corresponding to the number of the yellow bell;

sentences.zh: 隔下九寸，其空自小竅迤殺至管底，約徑二寸餘，蓋以聚其氣而上之。

translations.literal: Below the partition nine cun; its hollow from small aperture gradually tapered to tube bottom, approximately two cun odd in diameter — presumably to gather its qi and send it upward.
translations.idiomatic: Below the partition was nine cun; its hollow tapered gradually from the small aperture to the bottom of the tube, approximately a little more than two cun in diameter, presumably to gather the qi and send it upward.

sentences.zh: 其制與律家所說不同，蓋古所謂玉律者是也。

translations.literal: Its design differed from what pitch specialists describe — presumably the so-called jade pitch pipe of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Its design differed from what pitch specialists describe and was presumably the so-called jade pitch pipe of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 適遷他官，事遂寢，有志者深惜之。

translations.literal: Just then transferred to another office; matter then shelved; men of purpose deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Just then he was transferred to another office, and the matter was shelved — to the deep regret of men of purpose.

sentences.zh: 至順三年五月，贈翰林學士、資善大夫、上護軍，追封汝南郡公，諡文懿。

translations.literal: Third year of Zhishun fifth month, posthumously granted Hanlin Academician, Charitable Grand Master, Senior Guardian General; posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Runan Commandery; posthumous title Wanyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Zhishun he was posthumously granted Hanlin Academician, Charitable Grand Master, and Senior Guardian General; posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Runan Commandery; posthumous title Wanyi.
